Vectors from different embedding models cannot be compared, so a notebook records the model that
created it and refuses another one. Change models with `abstractnote rebuild --reembed` and the
new `--embed-base-url` / `--embed-model`: it replays notes and revisions into fresh stores with the
new vectors. See [troubleshooting.md](troubleshooting.md#this-notebook-is-pinned-to-the-embedding-model).

### Is anything ever deleted or truncated?

No. Notes are archived, never deleted (`POST /note/notes/{id}/archive`). Long notes are split
into sections for the model and merged before linking; the stored text and the full-text index
always keep the whole note. Superseded facts keep their history with a closed validity window.

### Does AbstractNote describe images and transcribe recordings?

It stores every attachment and reads text, Markdown and PDF files. Image descriptions and
transcripts need an image model and a speech model passed to the note tools
(`abstractnote.tools.bind(..., extractors={"vision": ..., "stt": ...})`); the gateway integration
does not configure them yet. Without them the note keeps the file and its details, and the capture
result carries a warning such as "Kept photo.jpg; no image model is configured to describe it."

### How large can an attachment be?

Uploads through a gateway follow the gateway's attachment limit (25 MB per file by default). Add
larger files on the machine that holds them with `abstractnote import files PATH`.

### How fast is processing?

Expect about two model calls per note. The gateway's processor handles up to 20 notes every two
minutes, one at a time per user, so a large import is understood over hours while live notes go
first (imports use the lowest priority). "Process now" in the web app starts a pass immediately.

### Can agents use my notebook?

Yes. Inside the gateway the note tools are bound to the caller's own notebook and auto-approved,
and `note-recall` also answers the `abstractcode.agent.v1` chat contract (`prompt` in,
`output.response` out). Agents should start a session with `note_changes` and cite the note ids
they rely on; see [remembering.md](remembering.md#for-agents-and-entities).

## Design questions

### Why not regular expressions for names and duplicates?

Identity and change are judged by a model from candidates; deterministic code only produces exact
hashes and candidate lists. See [ADR 0004](adr/0004-models-decide-identity-no-text-heuristics.md).

### Why two stores?

The revision log is the truth; the note index serves fast interactive reads and the AbstractMemory
store holds every claim as a temporal triple that framework tools can read. Both are projections
you can rebuild. See [data-model.md](data-model.md) and
[ADR 0003](adr/0003-revision-log-is-truth-index-and-abstractmemory-projection.md).

### Why is understanding queued instead of immediate?

Capture must never wait for a model. The queue gives priority order, retries and a visible state;
"Instant linking" in the web app processes a note right after capture when you want that. See
[ADR 0005](adr/0005-eventual-consistency-queue-and-processor-automation.md).

## Limits of this version

- The watch app has no TestFlight or App Store build yet; you build and install it from source
  ([watch/apple/BUILD.md](../watch/apple/BUILD.md)). The Python package (`pip install
  "abstractnote[gateway]"`) and the web app (`@abstractframework/note`) are published.
- How the Apple apps store the sign-in (a protected file in the app container) is proposed and
  awaits a ruling ([ADR 0006](adr/0006-apple-client-credential-storage.md)).
- The command line works on local notebooks only (no gateway client mode).
- The iPhone app is planned, not built ([clients.md](clients.md#iphone-app-phoneiphone)).

---

## docs/troubleshooting.md

# Troubleshooting

Each entry starts from what you see (a message, an exit code, a status), then gives the cause,
how to confirm it, and the fix. Setup steps are in [getting-started.md](getting-started.md), the
HTTP and CLI reference in [api.md](api.md), and short conceptual answers in [faq.md](faq.md).

The command line prints results as JSON on standard output and problems as one sentence on
standard error. Exit codes: `0` done, `2` bad input (the sentence says what to change), `3` a
part of AbstractNote that is not installed or not available in this version. `abstractnote
import` exits `1` when some records could not be imported (they are listed under `errors`).

## Notebook and embeddings

### This notebook is pinned to the embedding model

```text
This notebook is pinned to the embedding model 'abstractnote-hashing-v1-256' but the embedder given is 'text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b'; rebuild with reembed to change models.
```

- **Cause**: the notebook was created with one embedding model and the command gave another.
  `abstractnote-hashing-v1-256` is the built-in embedder used when the first command had no
  `--embed-base-url` / `--embed-model`.
- **Check**: `abstractnote status --notebook DIR` shows `embedding_pin.model_id`.
- **Fix**: give the pinned model's flags again, or move the notebook to the new model with
  `abstractnote rebuild --reembed --notebook DIR --embed-base-url URL --embed-model MODEL`.
  `status` then shows the new pin.

### This notebook's vectors were made with the embedding model ...

```text
This notebook's vectors were made with the embedding model 'text-embedding-qwen3-embedding-0.6b'; open it with that embedder ...
```

- **Cause**: the notebook is pinned to an embedding server and the command gave no
  `--embed-base-url` / `--embed-model`. The notebook then opens read-only: `status` (which shows
  `read_only` with this sentence), `entity`, `day`, `changes` and `search` work, and `search`
  matches words only and says so in its `warnings`. Commands that write or need new vectors
  (capture, processing, user actions, imports, rebuild) refuse with this sentence before writing
  anything.
- **Fix**: add the two flags with the pinned model to the command.
- **Imports**: `abstractnote import` takes the same two flags.

### Give both --embed-base-url and --embed-model

One of the two flags is missing. They always go together.

### Say which notebook with --notebook DIR

Every command except `bundle` needs `--notebook DIR`. A gateway keeps a user's notebook in
`<data dir>/users/<tenant>/<runtime>/abstractnote` (or `<data dir>/abstractnote` without user
accounts).

## Processing and models

### Give --provider and --model for the model that processes or answers

`process --local` and `search --effort standard|deep` run a model. Name it, for example
`--provider mlx --model mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit`.

### MLX dependencies not installed

```text
MLX dependencies not installed. Install with: pip install "abstractcore[apple]"
```

- **Cause**: `--provider mlx` needs the MLX engine, which is not part of the base AbstractCore
  install.
- **Fix**: `pip install "abstractcore[apple]"` in the same environment as `abstractnote` (on
  Apple silicon). On Linux with an NVIDIA or AMD GPU, use `abstractcore[gpu]`; anywhere else, use
  a provider that serves models over HTTP, such as `lmstudio` or `ollama`.

### Processing through a gateway is not available here

`abstractnote process` without `--local` (exit 3). Add `--local` with `--provider` and `--model`
to process on this machine, or use **Process now** in the web app's Settings to start the
gateway's processor.

### Gateway client mode is not available in this version

The command was given `--gateway`. Run it on the machine that holds the notebook with
`--notebook DIR`, or use the HTTP API ([api.md](api.md)).

### Creating the processor needs a gateway

`abstractnote processor ensure` (exit 3). Open the web app, which creates the processor when it
is missing, or call `POST /api/gateway/note/processor/ensure` with your account token.

### Notes stay queued

- **Check**: `abstractnote status` (or `GET /api/gateway/note/queue`) shows `queued`,
  `processing` and `failed`, and `automations.processor_id`.
- **Cause and fix**: with no `processor_id`, the processor automation does not exist yet: open
  the web app or call `processor/ensure` as above. When `automations.processor.healthy` is false (for
  example after an upgrade: `reason` names the old workflow version), the processor cannot run; open the
  web app (it repairs on load, or press Repair in Settings, Queue) or call `processor/ensure`, which
  replaces it. With a processor, notes are processed up to 20 every two minutes,
  one at a time, highest priority first; imports wait behind live notes by design. Headless, run
  `process --local` again until the queue is empty.

### A note failed to process

The queue retries a failed note after one minute and then after ten minutes; the third failure
marks it `failed` with the error. "Processing stopped before it finished." means a run ended
while it held the note (the lease expired). Fix the cause the error names (most often the model
or provider), then press **Retry** in the web app's queue panel or call
`POST /api/gateway/note/queue/{note_id}/retry`.

### the generated flows are stale

```text
the generated flows are stale (note-process); run python -m abstractnote.flows.build
```

`abstractnote bundle` found that the flow JSON in the package no longer matches the generator
(you changed a prompt, a schema or the generator). Run `python -m abstractnote.flows.build` and
commit the regenerated `src/abstractnote/flows/json/*.json`; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Gateway

### Every /api/gateway/note call answers 404, or the bundle is unknown

- **Cause**: the gateway does not have AbstractNote, or it is a gateway release without the
  AbstractNote seam (`abstractgateway.abstractnote_seam`). In that environment
  `python -c "import abstractnote.gateway"` fails with one sentence that names the missing seam.
- **Fix**: install `abstractnote` and the AbstractGateway checkout with the integration in the
  gateway's own environment, then restart the gateway
  ([getting-started.md](getting-started.md#3-the-gateway-path)). A signed-in
  `GET /api/gateway/note/status` then answers `200`.

### Your notebook is not available: ...

Every note tool answers this sentence when the gateway could not bind the tools to your
notebook; the rest of the gateway keeps working. The reason follows the colon. The most common
one is an embedding pin: the notebook was first used with a different embedding route than the
one the gateway has now. Rebuild it with the gateway's model (`abstractnote rebuild --reembed`
on the notebook directory, gateway stopped), or restore the earlier embedding route.

### A capture waits for approval

The watch app says "This note waits for your OK in AbstractNote on another device."; a headless
run raises "run ... waits for approval of [...]; note tools must be auto-approved".

- **Cause**: the note tools are not in the gateway's auto-approve set, so the runtime parks the
  run on a tool-approval wait. The integration adds them; a gateway without it, or a custom
  approval policy that replaced the set, does not.
- **Fix**: run the gateway with the AbstractNote integration and its default approval policy.
  Note tools only read and write the caller's own notebook.

### 409 automation_busy, "Already running."

```json
{"detail": {"reason_code": "automation_busy", "message": "An occurrence is already running or waiting to run."}}
```

**Process now** was pressed while a processing pass is running or queued. Nothing is wrong; the
running pass continues and the next one follows on schedule.

### 413, "Attachment too large"

```text
Attachment too large (26214401 bytes > 26214400 bytes)
```

The file is over the gateway's attachment limit (25 MB per file by default). The web app refuses
it before uploading: "This file is larger than 25 MB; add it from the computer that has it with:
abstractnote import files <folder>." Import it on that machine, or raise the gateway's limit.

### Local file paths are not accepted here

```text
Local file paths are not accepted here; upload the file as an attachment instead.
```

A `note-capture` run was given `{"path": ...}` in `context.attachments`. Inside a gateway the
note tools only read files you uploaded: call `POST /api/gateway/attachments/upload` and pass
`{"$artifact": "<id>"}`. Headless, paths are accepted only inside a folder you allow
(`abstractnote.tools.bind(..., allow_paths_under=DIR)`); outside it the answer is "That file is
outside the folder this notebook may read from."

### Run errors start with "Runtime error: "

A flow that refuses its input still completes; its output is `{"success": false, "error":
"Runtime error: <sentence>"}` with no `response`. The sentence after the prefix is the cause
(for example the path refusal above). Clients strip the prefix before showing it.

### 401 Unauthorized, "You were signed out. Please sign in again."

The token or session is no longer valid (revoked, expired, or for another gateway). Sign in
again with a `user` account token or an emailed code. Admin tokens are not meant for clients.

### 404 "That note is not in your notebook."

The id belongs to another account's notebook or does not exist. Each account sees only its own
notebook, by design.

### The web app says "Your notebook cannot show this yet."

The gateway answered 501: the installed `abstractnote` lacks a read the web app asks for.
Install the same version of `abstractnote` on the gateway as the web app expects, then restart
the gateway.

## Attachments

### Kept the file, but its text could not be read

Capture results carry warnings such as "Kept photo.jpg; no image model is configured to
describe it.", "Kept the recording memo.m4a with its details; no speech model is configured to
transcribe it." or "Kept report.pdf; its text could not be read here (PDF reading is not
installed on this machine)." The file is always stored and linked to the note; only its text is
missing. Image descriptions and transcripts need the extractors described in
[faq.md](faq.md#does-abstractnote-describe-images-and-transcribe-recordings).

---

## docs/data-model.md

# Data model

This page defines the records AbstractNote keeps, how time works, how identities are assigned,
and how duplicates are handled. The Python types live in `abstractnote.model`; the SQLite schema
in `abstractnote.store.schema`; the AbstractMemory projection in `abstractnote.store.kg`.

## Overview

```mermaid
erDiagram
    NOTE ||--o{ ATTACHMENT : has
    NOTE ||--o| QUEUE_ITEM : "waits in"
    NOTE ||--o{ REVISION : causes
    REVISION ||--o{ CLAIM : adds
    REVISION ||--o{ ENTITY : "creates or changes"
    ENTITY ||--o{ ALIAS : "known as"
    CLAIM }o--|| ENTITY : subject
    CLAIM }o--o| ENTITY : object
    ENTITY ||--o{ RELATION : "linked by"
    NOTE ||--o{ TASK : mentions
    NOTE }o--o{ TOPIC : "filed under"
    INSIGHT }o--o{ NOTE : "evidenced by"
    COMMUNITY ||--o{ ENTITY : groups
```

## Note

A note is anything you send: a sentence, a document, an image, a recording, a video, a log, a
chat turn imported from a transcript. It is the unit of provenance: every entity, claim and
revision points back to the note(s) that caused it.

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `note_id` | `nt_<26 chars>` | Deterministic, base32 of a sha256. Imports: `sha256(importer, source_key)`. Live capture: `sha256(idempotency_key)` when the client sends one (clients always should; the runs API has no idempotency key of its own), otherwise `sha256(text_norm, attachment hashes, occurred_at to the minute, source.client)`. A retried request yields the same note; the same words said again on another day yield a new note that revisits the earlier one. |
| `kind` | enum | `idea`, `task`, `decision`, `fact`, `event`, `question`, `reflection`, `reference`, `log`, `conversation`, `personal`, `synthesis`, `insight`. Assigned by the quick filing step; `synthesis` and `insight` are system-authored. |
| `title` | text | Short title (model-written or taken from the source). |
| `text` | text | The note body as received (Markdown allowed). Never truncated. |
| `text_norm` | text | Whitespace-normalised, lower-cased copy used for hashing and full-text search. |
| `summary` | text | One to three sentences written by the processor. |
| `occurred_at` | ISO 8601 UTC | When the note was made or the event happened. From the client clock, the importer (message timestamp, file date, EXIF), the attachment's own metadata date for a capture that gives none, or an explicit value; moved only by a `note.redate` (see Time). |
| `date_basis`, `date_approximate` | read only | How `occurred_at` was found (`GET /note/notes/{id}`): the latest redate's basis (`content`, `user`), else the importer's `source.origin.date_basis` (docs/importers.md), else `client` for a live note and `unrecorded` for an older import; `date_approximate` is true for a stand-in date (`file_mtime`, `git_added`, `bulk_commit`, `store_updated`, `last_record`, `origin_session`, `front_matter_modified`, `unrecorded`), the ones a client offers to "Set the date". |
| `received_at` | ISO 8601 UTC | When AbstractNote stored it. |
| `processed_at` | ISO 8601 UTC or null | When the last successful revision was applied. |
| `source` | object | Provenance: `{client: web|watch|iphone|cli|agent|importer, importer?: claude-sessions|agora|markdown|files, origin: {...source-specific ids...}, author?: user id or agent name}`. |
| `location` | object or null | `{lat, lon, accuracy_m?, label?}` when the client provides one. |
| `language` | text or null | BCP-47 tag detected by the filing step. |
| `topics` | list | Categories assigned by filing and refined by processing (see Topics). |
| `priority` | int 0..3 | 3 urgent, 2 high, 1 normal, 0 bulk. |
| `status` | enum | `received`, `queued`, `processing`, `processed`, `failed`, `duplicate`, `archived`. |
| `duplicate_of` | note id or null | Set only when the same idempotency key or import source key arrives again (a retry), never for the same words on another occasion. |
| `session_id`, `run_id` | text | The gateway session and the run that captured it, when applicable. |
| `archived_at` | ISO or null | Notes are archived, never deleted. |

### Attachment

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `attachment_id` | `at_<...>` deterministic from `(note_id, sha256)` |
| `sha256`, `size`, `mime`, `filename` | the bytes' identity |
| `artifact_ref` | the gateway artifact that carried it, when uploaded through the gateway |
| `blob_path` | `blobs/<sha256[:2]>/<sha256>`; stored once per distinct content across the notebook |
| `extracted_text`, `extracted_by` | text derived from the bytes (document text, transcript, image description, log excerpt, media metadata) and which extractor produced it (`plain`, `markdown`, `pdf`, `vision:<model>`, `stt:<model>`, `media-metadata`, `none`). Audio and video with a speech track are transcribed when a speech model is configured; otherwise, and for music, the filing keeps the metadata (filename, duration, tags) and the capture answer says so plainly. |

Two notes that attach the same file share one blob; the second attachment records the
relation `same_bytes_as` so the graph shows that the file came back.

## Entity

An entity is a thing the notes talk about: a person, an organisation, a project, a concept, a
place, an event, an artifact (a document, a dataset, a repository), a piece of software, or a
generic thing.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `entity_id` | `ex:<kind>-<slug>` following AbstractFramework ADR 0025, the slug being the canonical name written in kebab-case ASCII (`ex:person-laurent-philippe-albou`). A collision with a different entity of the same kind appends `-2`, `-3`. Ids are never reused. |
| `kind` | `person`, `org`, `project`, `concept`, `place`, `event`, `artifact`, `software`, `thing` |
| `name` | the one canonical name, shown everywhere: Unicode NFKC, trimmed, case-folded, every run of whitespace, punctuation or underscores collapsed to one `_` (snake_case for several words), none at either end (`ids.canonical_name`: `Laurent-Philippe Albou` is `laurent_philippe_albou`; `Memory`, `memory` and `MEMORY.` are `memory`) |
| `name_key` | the lookup key of the name (`ids.name_key`, equal to the canonical name); unique among live entities, so a person never sees two entities that differ only by case, spacing or punctuation |
| `display_name` | the first surface form a note wrote (`Laurent-Philippe Albou`), kept for clients that want it; a rename replaces it |
| `aliases` | other names seen in notes, each stored with its surface form and its key (`alias_key`); shown once per canonical name and never the entity's own; exact matching is by key |
| `summary` | one model-written sentence saying what the notebook knows about it, rewritten when a note tells something new (each revision kept) |
| `first_seen`, `last_seen` | `occurred_at` of the first and latest note mentioning it |
| `note_count` | number of notes that mention it |
| `merged_into` | set when the model decided this entity is the same as another; the record stays so old links still resolve |
| `embedding` | vector of `name + aliases + summary`, refreshed when the summary changes |

Entities are created only by revisions. The id is minted from the canonical name of the name chosen
by the model at creation time; later renames add aliases and may change `name`, never the id.

One canonical name per entity is a deterministic guarantee, applied when a revision is applied
(`Notebook.apply_revision`, `abstractnote.store.names`): an `entity.create` whose canonical name a
live entity already has becomes a reuse of that entity, whatever the model decided. The surface forms
become its aliases, later ops of the revision follow it (an identical statement reinforces the
existing one, a statement linking the entity to itself is left out), the revision records a warning
(with `kind_conflict` when the kinds differ: the existing kind is kept, never a second entity), and
the stored revision is the rewritten one, so a replay agrees. A rename onto a canonical name another
live entity has is refused (that is a merge). Aliases never force a reuse: an alias is the model's
word for an entity, and only produces candidates. A mention name or alias that ends with one of the
entity kinds in parentheses (`memory (software)`) loses that suffix before its canonical name is
taken, with a warning (`names.strip_kind_suffix`): the linking packet once showed entities as
`name (kind)` and the model copied the form into names; it now shows `name — kind`. This is
structural (a known kind word in a fixed position), not a reading of the name.

Notebooks written before canonical names (schema 1) are upgraded on open: `name_key`, `display_name`
and `alias_key` are filled in, a later live entity whose canonical name an earlier one holds is marked
(`key_clash_with`), and the next processed note runs the repair, `Notebook.normalize_entities`
(`abstractnote normalize`, `POST /note/entities/normalize`): each group of live entities sharing a
canonical name is merged into its earliest entity, one `entity.merge` revision per merged entry with
source `{client, account}` (`migration` for the automatic run), the merged entry's names kept as
aliases. Reads follow merges, so its statements, relations, notes and tasks come with it; an unmerge
undoes it, and the separated entry takes the first free `<name>_2`, `<name>_3` so two live entities
never share a canonical name. A pair a person separated is never joined again by the repair. The
repair also joins the entries left by the `name (kind)` echo: a live entity whose surface form ends
with ` (<kind>)` and whose canonical name is `<name>_<kind>` is merged into the live entity named
`<name>` when there is one (the group lists it under `kind_suffix`; the echoed form is not kept as an
alias); an entry written as words (`contact person`) or whose plain name no entity has is left alone.

## Claim

A claim is one statement with time and provenance. Claims are the edges and attributes of the
graph.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `claim_id` | `cl_<...>` deterministic from `(note_id, subject, predicate, object)`; predicate CURIEs keep their case in the index |
| `subject_id` | entity id |
| `predicate` | a CURIE from the AbstractSemantics registry when one fits (`schema:knowsAbout`, `schema:participant`, `skos:related`, `dcterms:references`, `cito:disagreesWith`, ...), otherwise `ex:<snake_case>` |
| `object_id` or `object_literal` | an entity, or a literal value (text, number, date) |
| `certainty` | `stated`, `probable`, `possible`, `reported`, `disputed` (tokens, not numbers) |
| `stance` | `assert`, `revise`, `retract`: what the note does to earlier knowledge |
| `observed_at` | the note's `occurred_at` |
| `valid_from`, `valid_until` | the validity window; `valid_from` defaults to `observed_at` for state claims and is null for timeless facts or for a statement that stopped before its note was written (`valid_until` earlier than the note); `valid_until` is set when a later note supersedes or retracts the claim, when the claim is an earlier belief placed before a later one (`claim.insert_before`: the later one's start), and equals `valid_from` when you retract it ("never true"); it is never earlier than `valid_from` |
| `status` | `active`, `superseded`, `retracted` |
| `superseded_by` | the claim that replaced it |
| `evidence` | the verbatim excerpt of the note that supports the claim |
| `note_id`, `revision_id` | provenance |
| `assertion_id` | the id of the same claim in the AbstractMemory store (equals `claim_id`) |

### Relation

A relation is a derived, fast-to-read summary of all claims between two entities:
`(subject_id, object_id, predicate) -> first_seen, last_seen, count, active_claim_ids`. The graph
view reads relations. The **relation timeline** (`/note/relations/{a}/{b}`) is first-class: all
claims between two entities in history order, with supersessions and a then-versus-now of the
relationship, so the evolution of a link is as visible as the evolution of a node.

## Revision

A revision is the append-only record of what one processed note did to the graph. It is the
authoritative history: replaying revisions in order rebuilds entities, claims, relations, topics
and tasks.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `revision_id` | `rv_<...>` deterministic from `(note_id, attempt)`; user actions use `(action, target, occurred_at)` |
| `note_id` | the cause (null for a user action; then `source` names the client and account) |
| `applied_index`, `applied_kg` | flags set after each projection commits; recovery replays revisions whose flags are not both set (idempotent thanks to deterministic ids) |
| `at` | the note's `occurred_at` (history time) |
| `recorded_at` | when the processor applied it (system time) |
| `run_id` | the processing run (ledger) |
| `ops` | ordered list of operations |
| `summary` | one sentence written by the processor ("Linked the LUT budget decision to Castor; superseded the earlier plan.") |

Operations:

| op | payload |
|---|---|
| `entity.create` | `{entity_id, kind, name, aliases, summary}` |
| `entity.alias` | `{entity_id, alias}` |
| `entity.rename` | `{entity_id, name, previous}` |
| `entity.summary` | `{entity_id, summary, previous}` |
| `entity.merge` | `{from_id, into_id, reason}` |
| `claim.add` | the claim |
| `claim.supersede` | `{claim_id, by_claim_id, reason, valid_until}` |
| `claim.retract` | `{claim_id, reason, valid_until?}` (without `valid_until`, the window closes at the revision's time) |
| `claim.reinforce` | `{claim_id, note_id}` (the same statement seen again) |
| `claim.insert_before` | `{claim_id, before_claim_id, valid_until, reason, after_claim_id?, after_valid_until?}`: the claim just added by this revision comes from a note older than `before_claim_id`, the belief it gives way to; it is closed at `valid_until` (that belief's start) and superseded by it, which stays untouched; `after_claim_id`, the belief before it, now ends at `after_valid_until` (this claim's start) and is superseded by it (see Time) |
| `topic.assign` | `{note_id, topic}` (stored under the topic's canonical name; processing keeps the first 3 per note) |
| `topic.unassign` | `{note_id, topic}`: the note leaves the topic as stored (`abstractnote normalize-topics`) |
| `task.open` / `task.close` / `task.drop` | `{task_id, text, due?, by_note_id?}` |
| `entity.unmerge` | `{entity_id, from_id, reason}` (a user action; re-points the claims that came from `from_id`) |
| `entity.mention` | `{entity_id, note_id}` (the note talks about the entity; drives `note_count`, `first_seen`, `last_seen`) |
| `note.summary` | `{note_id, summary, kind, language}` |
| `note.archive` | `{note_id, duplicate_of?, reason?}`: the note is archived (it leaves lists, search and the queue, keeps its links) and names the copy it duplicates (`abstractnote dedupe-sources`) |
| `note.redate` | `{note_id, from, to, basis, quote?, reason?}`: the note moves in history time (`basis` `content` when its text states its date, `user` when a person sets it); its mentions, its topics' ranges, its queue place, and the statements and tasks it wrote with the old date move with it; `source.redated` keeps `{basis, from, to, revision_id}` |

User actions (`close a task`, `retract a claim`, `undo a merge`, `confirm a match`) produce revisions with
`source = {client, account}` and no note; they are the human side of an actionable graph. Through
the gateway, `account` is the signed-in user and `client` is `web` (the Note web app) or `api`
(any other caller), decided by the server, never by the request body.

Confirming a match from the review list (`POST /note/review/{id}/confirm`) is a revision with `action =
match.confirm` and `target` = the review id: for a close match (an `unsure` decision, recorded as a `skos:closeMatch`
claim from the new entry to the candidate) its ops are `entity.merge` (the new entry into the candidate) and
`claim.supersede` of the close-match claim; for a merge the processor made it has no ops and only records that you
keep it. Revisions are the truth, so a rebuild keeps what you confirmed.

Reversibility: a merge keeps both records and can be undone by a later revision that re-points
claims; a supersession keeps the old claim with its window closed.

## Topic

A topic is a lightweight category (`#lut`, `#release`, `#family`). The filing step chooses from
existing topics first and proposes new ones sparingly; the processor may refine. Topics are
flat; entities carry the structure.

A topic is stored under its canonical name (the entity rule: `Bug-Fix`, `bug fix` and `bug_fix` are
`bug_fix`), and processing keeps the first 3 topics the model lists for a note (`TOPICS_PER_NOTE`; a
user revision is not capped); the others are named, never dropped silently (ADR 0007): the revision's result
lists them under `topics_not_assigned`, its warnings and its summary say which were not kept. Quick filing keeps
4 (`MAX_FILING_TOPICS`) and names the rest in `note_file`'s `topics_not_assigned`. The extraction packet lists the 50 most used topics. Topics stored before
that keep their spelling until `abstractnote normalize-topics --notebook DIR [--dry-run]` gives each
group one name in ONE revision (`topic.unassign` + `topic.assign`): the same canonical name (case,
`-`, `_` and whitespace). That is spelling, not meaning: no word rule decides that two topics are one
(ADR 0004), so `bug_fixes` and `bug_fix`, or `gateway` and `abstractgateway`, stay two topics. Search and
note lists filter by a topic's given and canonical spelling.

## Task

Open loops extracted from notes: `{task_id, note_id, text, status open|done|dropped, due?,
closed_by_note_id?}`; `task_id` is `tk_<...>` deterministic from `(note_id, normalised text)`. A later note that reports the task done closes it with a `task.close` op,
decided by the model during processing, applied only when the linking quotes the note's own words that say it is
done (`evidence`, a whole-word sequence of the note) and the note is not older than the task; otherwise the open task
stays open and the note's task is its own (opened, and closed when reported done), with a warning. So no task closes
before it opened.

## Insight

System-authored notes with `kind = insight` or `synthesis`: dossiers from deep recall and the
findings of the reflect flow (open loops, contradictions, resurfaced material, connections).
They carry `evidence_note_ids`, `entity_ids`, `insight_kind` (`warning`, `reminder`,
`connection`, `contradiction`, `evolution`, `dossier`, `cue`) and `acked_at`. Cue cards are the
unacknowledged insights other than dossiers, newest first.

## Community

A community is a group of entities the notes keep bringing together (a project and its people, a set
of tools, a theme), found by `abstractnote.recall.communities` without a model and named by one. They
make a large graph readable: the explorer colours nodes by community, and the statistics count them.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `community_id` | `cm_<20 chars>`, a hash of the sorted member entity ids when the community first appeared; kept while its membership changes little (below) |
| `label`, `summary`, `kind` | the model's name (at most 4 words), one sentence on what holds the group together, and `project`, `theme`, `people`, `tooling`, `process` or `other`; null until the reflect flow labels it |
| `size`, `top_entities` | member count and the 5 members with the most notes |
| `created_at`, `labelled_at` | when it first appeared, when it was last labelled |
| `stale_label` | the label is kept but more than 20 % of the membership changed since it was labelled: the next reflect run names it again |
| `revision_count_at_compute` | applied revisions when detection last ran; `GET /note/communities` reports `revisions_since` |

Detection is Louvain (`networkx`, fixed seed, resolution 1.0 by default) over the live entities,
deterministic for a given networkx version: the same graph under the same networkx release gives the
same communities, but another release may split it differently, so `meta.communities` records the
`networkx` version of each computation (`GET /note/communities` reports it) and the dependency is
capped below the first release that changes the partition (`networkx>=3.2,<3.7`; 3.4 and 3.6 were tested, 3.7 differs);
the weight of a pair is the number of its statements that were not retracted (merged entries count
for their survivor) plus a co-mention weight: each note that mentions `k >= 2` live entities adds
`1/((k-1)·log2 k)` to every pair among them, so a long note weighs `k/(2·log2 k)` in all rather than
`k/2` (docs/cognition.md, note-reflect). Groups of fewer than 3 entities are the **loose ends**
and belong to no community. A recomputation matches each new group to the previous community it
overlaps most (Jaccard of the member sets, best overlaps first, each previous community used once):
an overlap of at least 0.6 keeps the id, label, summary and kind; anything else is a new community
with a new id and no label. Once after the networkx version changed (or after a computation that
recorded none), the floor is 0.5, and a labelled previous community that still matches nothing hands
its label, marked stale, to the unmatched new group it overlaps most (a new id); the recompute
response lists those labels under `carry_over` (`kept`, `stale`, and `dropped` for a label no new
group overlaps), so a library upgrade never loses a label silently. Tables `communities` and `entity_communities` (one row per member) are
derived, but because the labels are model work, `rebuild` keeps them (`schema.KEPT_TABLES`). A
notebook opened without its embedding model reads communities and refuses to recompute or label.

A community's label longer than 4 words is kept whole with an `over_length` warning (ADR 0007).

## Consolidation run

Table `consolidation_runs` (kept by `rebuild`) holds one row per memory consolidation (docs/cognition.md,
note-consolidate); the open row has no `finished_at`. `status` is `running`, `completed` (nothing was left out),
`completed_with_gaps` (the run finished its stages but left items for the next one), `failed` (`error` is the
step's sentence) or `interrupted` (it stopped before closing). `stages_json` holds per stage `{done, total,
seconds_per_item, started_at, skipped?, reason?, reasons?, skipped_ids?: [{id, reason}]}`: `skipped_ids` are the
entries or groups the stage skipped for this run after the model left them unanswered twice. `results_json`
holds the counts and, for a finished run, `left_out: {summaries, labels, reasons}` (skipped items still pending
at the close plus what the time budget did not reach, never more than pending) and `budget_spent`.
`offered_json` lists the entries the run already offered (never offered twice in a run), `touched_json` the
entries it merged into or summarised. A summary longer than 600 characters is kept whole with an `over_length`
warning in its revision (ADR 0007).

## Time

AbstractNote is bitemporal, and every note carries three dates that answer three different questions:

| Date | Field | Question it answers |
|---|---|---|
| Authored (history time) | `occurred_at`, `claim.observed_at`, `revision.at` | "When was this written or did it happen?" "What did the graph look like on day X?" |
| Valid | `claim.valid_from`, `claim.valid_until` | "What did I believe about X at time T?" |
| Archive-accepted (system time) | `received_at` (and `processed_at`, `revision.recorded_at`) | "What did my archive hold on date R?" "What has the processor done since I last looked?" |

The axes are independent: an import received today can hold notes authored years ago, and a note
written in January can say something stopped being true in March.

Rules:

- The archive **as received at R** (`as_received=R` on `GET /note/graph`, `GET /note/entities/{id}`,
  `GET /note/changes` and `GET /note/day/{date}`) = only the notes with `received_at <= R`, so material
  imported later is left out even when it was authored earlier. What derives from notes follows them: a
  revision belongs when the note that caused it was received by R (a user action without a note: when it was
  recorded by R); entities exist when such a revision created them or such a note mentions them; merges,
  names, aliases, summaries and the closing of claims count only when their revision belongs, so a claim a
  later note superseded reads as it stood before. `at` and `as_received` compose: "the graph as of T, from
  what the archive held on R".
- The graph **as of T** = entities first seen at or before T (their creating revision's `at`, or an
  earlier note that mentions them when notes are processed out of history order), not merged away
  by T; edges from claims with `observed_at <= T`.
- **Beliefs at T** = claims with `valid_from <= T` and (`valid_until` is null or `> T`).
- Supersession sets `valid_until` of the old claim to the `occurred_at` of the superseding note;
  so does a note whose stance is `retract`.
- A retraction you make (`POST /note/claims/{id}/retract`) says the claim was never true: its
  status becomes `retracted` and `valid_until = valid_from` (its `observed_at` when it has no
  start), an empty window, never the moment you said so. Retracted claims are never beliefs.
- Importers set `occurred_at` from the source (message timestamp, commit date, file date);
  `received_at` is always the ingest time, so an import is visible as a system-time event while
  history stays truthful.
- Explicit time references inside a note ("last Tuesday", "in 2024") are extracted as claims with
  literal dates when the model can resolve them from the note's own `occurred_at`; they never
  move the note itself. Only the date the text gives ITSELF can (below).

### Retrospective insertion

Notes and archives from earlier dates (and other projects that name known entities) keep arriving into a graph
built from later ones, while live notes arrive too. History adapts; nothing is rewritten in place except windows:

- **Beliefs in history order.** Supersession and contradiction are applied with regard to time. For a statement
  `C_new` (its note's `occurred_at` = `t_new`) that the linking says supersedes an existing `C_old` (`observed_at`
  = `t_old`), on the same resolved subject and predicate:
  - `t_new >= t_old`: as always, `C_old` closes at `t_new` (`claim.supersede`, or `claim.retract` for a
    `retract` stance).
  - `t_new < t_old`: an older note never closes a later belief. `C_new` is inserted as the EARLIER belief
    (`claim.add` + `claim.insert_before`): placed in its interval of the supersession lineage of `C_old` (the
    claims linked to it by `superseded_by`, same subject and predicate, retracted ones left out), it ends at the
    start of the next later belief and is superseded by it; the belief before it, if its window covered `t_new`,
    now ends at `t_new` and is superseded by `C_new`. Out of order 2026, then 2022, then 2024: 2022 holds
    [2022, 2024), 2024 holds [2024, 2026), 2026 is the active belief.
  - `contradicts` with `t_new < t_old` is the earlier belief the same way, unless the model marked the statement
    `disputed` and the two dates are at most 30 days apart: then it is a dispute (both kept, marked disputed).
  - A window never ends before it starts: a closing date earlier than the closed claim's `valid_from` closes it
    empty (at `valid_from`), in the builder (so the note index and AbstractMemory agree) and again in the
    projection (for replays of earlier revisions); an extracted end before an extracted start is ignored.
- **Tasks**: an older note cannot close a task opened later; a later note can (see Task).
- **Entities**: `first_seen` moves back to the older note (it is the earliest mention); the graph as of T shows
  the entity from then.
- **Retrospective marks** (`meta.retro`, written in the projection transaction): a note that mentions an entity
  already seen more than a day later (live notes a few minutes out of order are not), a `claim.insert_before` (its subject, object and neighbours) or a `note.redate`
  marks the entities: their summaries are stale (until a summary recorded after the mark is the current one, the
  consolidation's refresh), their then-versus-now cards are dropped, `graph_version` is bumped and the event is
  logged. `Notebook.retro_state()` reports `{graph_version, insertions, stale_summaries, retro_notes_since_communities,
  communities_due}` (due after 20 retrospective notes since the communities were last computed);
  `Notebook.after_retro_insert(entity_ids)` records one by hand. The revision result lists `retrospective` (the
  marked entities) and `claims_inserted_before`.
- **History order everywhere history is shown**: timelines, then-versus-now and relation timelines order by
  `occurred_at`/`observed_at` and end a superseded belief at its `valid_until` (not when the closing revision was
  applied); new entities are counted where they were first seen. `GET /note/changes` stays in system time.

### Document dates

A note's date can be a stand-in: a file's modification time, a commit, a session start, a store update. When the
date basis is approximate (`date_approximate`), the extraction header says so and the model may give
`document_date` `{iso, basis: "stated in the text", quote}`: the date the text gives itself (a dated letter, a
report's date line). At apply time it is used only when the quote is the note's own words (a whole-word sequence),
the date is not in the future and it differs from `occurred_at` by more than a day: the revision's first op is
`note.redate {from, to, basis: "content", quote}`, and the revision, its statements (`observed_at`, `valid_from`)
and its mentions carry the stated date; the basis becomes `content`. A live note (basis `client`) or a note with an
exact basis (`record`, `message`, `front_matter`, `exif`, `pdf_created` ...) is never redated from its text.

A person can set the date: `POST /note/notes/{id}/redate {occurred_at, reason}` is a user revision (`action
note.redate`, source `{client, account}`) with one `note.redate` op, basis `user`. Its mentions, statements and
tasks that carried the old date move in the note index; AbstractMemory keeps the statements' original
`observed_at` and `valid_from` (its content is append-only), so a person's redate of an already-understood note is
reflected in the note index and the graph views, and in the triple store only through later revisions.

## Identity and de-duplication

| Level | Mechanism | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Bytes | `sha256` of attachment content | one blob per content; later attachments link to it |
| Retry | same idempotency key (live) or source key (import) | same `note_id`, status `duplicate`, nothing else written |
| Same words again | exact `text_norm` hash equal to an earlier note | a new note; the earlier one is the strongest `ex:revisits` candidate; the answer says "you noted this on <date>" |
| Near-duplicate note | vector cosine over note embeddings, threshold 0.92 | kept as a distinct note, linked with `ex:revisits` to the earlier one: a revisit is a signal, not noise |
| Same canonical name | `name_key` of the mention's name equal to a live entity's: deterministic normalisation (case, spacing, punctuation, NFKC), not an identity judgement | always the first candidate; a create of that name is filed under the existing entity at apply time (warning, `kind_conflict` when the kinds differ); older notebooks repaired by `normalize_entities` |
| Entity | candidates from exact key match on names and aliases (`name_key`, `alias_key`), full-text on name and aliases, vector k-nearest on entity embeddings; the model decides `same`, `different`, `unsure` per mention and may propose a merge of two existing entities (`Gateway` versus `abstractgateway` is this level) | `entity.create`, `entity.alias`, `entity.merge` ops |
| Model merge (guard) | a proposed merge is applied only when the two entities have the same kind, share a name or alias key, the merged entry has fewer than 5 notes and neither was merged earlier in the same note (no chains); structural checks, never a reading of the names | otherwise a `skos:closeMatch` claim from the entry to merge to the other: a review item ("kept for review"), confirmed by a person |
| Values are not entities | a mention whose whole name is a bare number, a version (`0.9.0`, `v15`), a message or thread id (`c1234`, `dm#7`, `dm:a--b`), a link, an invite or hash token, or one word of the editable list `abstractnote/process/generic_words.txt` (`time`, `model`, `provider`, `triggers` ...): shape checks and an explicit list (operator ruling 2026-10-20), never a reading of meaning | never an entity: its statements keep it as a literal object (a statement whose subject it is is left out), with a warning |
| Claim | same `(subject, predicate, object)` after resolution | `claim.reinforce` instead of a new claim |
| Conflicting claim | same `(subject, predicate)` with a different object and the model marks the predicate single-valued, or the note's stance is `revise` or `retract`; a `supersedes` or `contradicts` naming a statement on another resolved subject or predicate is refused (a new statement, with a warning) | `claim.supersede` or `claim.retract` with reason, or `claim.insert_before` when the note is older (Time); history kept |

No regular-expression or keyword heuristics decide identity. Deterministic steps only produce
candidates, exact-hash matches and the canonical name key (ADR 0004, amended).

## AbstractMemory projection

Every claim is written to the AbstractMemory store as a `TripleAssertion`:

| TripleAssertion field | Value |
|---|---|
| `assertion_id` | `claim_id` |
| `subject`, `predicate`, `object` | entity ids and predicate CURIE; literal objects marked with `attributes.literal = true` so case is preserved |
| `scope`, `owner_id` | `global`, `abstractnote` |
| `observed_at` | the claim's `observed_at` (note time) |
| `valid_from`, `valid_until` | the claim's window |
| `confidence` | mapped from certainty: stated 0.9, probable 0.7, possible 0.5, reported 0.6, disputed 0.3 |
| `provenance` | `{source: "abstractnote", note_id, revision_id, run_id, evidence_quote, recorded_at}` |
| `attributes` | `{subject_type, object_type, certainty, stance, literal?, evidence_quote?, abstractnote_kind}` (`abstractnote_kind` is `claim`, `name`, `alias` or `same_as`) |

Entity names and aliases are written as `(entity_id, schema:name, "Name")` and
`(entity_id, skos:altLabel, "Alias")`; merges as `(from_id, schema:sameAs, into_id)`. Supersession
closes the old assertion in place with `close_assertion(assertion_id, valid_until)`, an additive
AbstractMemory store method introduced for this purpose (it updates `valid_until` only when it is
still open and leaves everything else untouched), and records a journal
`ClosureRecord(kind="supersede")` so both `TripleQuery(active_at=...)` and ranked retrieval agree
with the note index. A `claim.insert_before` closes the OLDER copy the same way (never the later belief), and moves
the window of the belief before it back with `ClaimStore.narrow_assertion` (`valid_until` only, earlier only, with
its own closure record): AbstractMemory has no public method for an already-closed window yet, so AbstractNote
writes that one column of its own triple store's table (a seam: an additive AbstractMemory method should replace it). AbstractMemory lowercases subjects, predicates and objects that are not
literals; the note index keeps the original case, and every AbstractMemory query from AbstractNote
passes `owner_id="abstractnote"`.

Write order for one revision: the revision row (intent) first, then the index projection (one
transaction that also sets `applied_index`), then the AbstractMemory projection, then `applied_kg`.
A revision whose index projection raises is set aside (nothing applied) instead of replayed. Embeddings are computed once in the
note index and handed to the triple store, so a rebuild never re-embeds over the network unless
`rebuild --reembed` is requested (for example after the embedding model changed; the pin is shown
by `GET /note/status`).

Store: `SQLiteTripleStore` at `<plane>/abstractnote/kg.sqlite3` with the notebook's embedder
(the gateway's embedding route inside a gateway; headless, the OpenAI-compatible model given on
the command line or the built-in hashing embedder; vectors are pinned to that embedding space and
handed over from the note index) and a `SQLiteJournal` in the same file (tables `memj_*`). A
notebook opened without the embedder it is pinned to opens read-only: reads and word-only search
work, and anything that would write or embed refuses with a plain sentence. A retraction (user
action or a note's `retract` stance) closes the assertion
the same way with `ClosureRecord(kind="retract")`; an undone merge closes its `schema:sameAs`.

---

## docs/cognition.md

# Cognition: the flows, the queue, the schemas

AbstractNote's thinking is written as AbstractFlow workflows (VisualFlow JSON) packaged in the
`abstractnote` bundle. They run on AbstractRuntime inside the gateway, one durable run per
invocation, and you can open every one of them in the Flow editor. Deterministic work happens in
plane-bound **note tools**; judgement happens in `llm_call` nodes with structured output.

Flow sources are generated by `abstractnote.flows.build` (a Python generator in the style of
AbstractFlow's `wf_common`) into `src/abstractnote/flows/json/*.json`; the bundle is packed by
`abstractnote bundle`. Only catalog node types are used.

## The flows

| Flow id | Interface | Started by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `note-capture` | `abstractnote.capture.v1` | clients, per note | store, de-duplicate, file quickly, answer, enqueue; optionally process inline |
| `note-process` | internal subflow | `note-capture` (inline) and `note-drain` | understand one note and revise the graph |
| `note-drain` | `abstractnote.drain.v1` | the processor automation, "Process now", the CLI | lease queued notes by priority and process them one at a time |
| `note-recall` | `abstractnote.recall.v1` and `abstractcode.agent.v1` | clients, agents, per question | answer a question at the requested effort |
| `note-mine` | internal subflow | `note-recall` (deep) | multi-step mining across time; writes a dossier insight |
| `note-reflect` | `abstractnote.reflect.v1` | a scheduled automation | surface open loops, contradictions, resurfaced material, connections |
| `note-consolidate` | `abstractnote.consolidate.v1` | the consolidation automation, "Consolidate now" | merge duplicates, refresh the groups and their names, stale summaries and then-and-now, then reflect |

Every flow exposes `provider` and `model` start pins. Blank means the gateway's default text
model. The processor automation carries the user's "filing model" (a small fast model is
recommended, for example `mlx-community/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-4bit` on Apple silicon); the reflect and
consolidation automations and recall at standard and deep effort use the user's "answering model". The
automations take the models from the notebook settings when they are created.

### note-capture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S[on_flow_start<br/>text, title?, occurred_at?, location?, source?,<br/>priority?, process_inline?, provider?, model?<br/>context.attachments] --> C[tool note_capture]
    C --> D{status}
    D -- duplicate --> M1[answer_user<br/>Already saved on date; link] --> E1[on_flow_end]
    D -- new --> Q[llm_call quick filing<br/>resp_schema QuickFiling]
    Q --> F[tool note_file<br/>title, kind, topics, urgency, language]
    F --> M2[answer_user<br/>Saved as kind 'title'. Related: ...]
    M2 --> I{process_inline?}
    I -- no --> E2[on_flow_end<br/>response, note_id, status=queued]
    I -- yes --> P[subflow note-process]
    P --> E3[on_flow_end<br/>response, note_id, status=processed, revision]
```

- `note_capture` reads attachments from the run's artifacts (inside the gateway, only
  `{"$artifact": id}` references resolved through the host's artifact store; local paths exist only
  in headless use with an allowed root), hashes bytes and text, stores the note and blobs, extracts
  text from documents and transcripts, returns `status` (`new` or `duplicate` for a retried
  idempotency key), the revisited notes (same words earlier) and similar notes (vector neighbours),
  the existing topics, and enqueues the note with the requested or default priority. The bound tool
  stamps `source.account` with the plane's account at bind time; `session_id` comes from a start
  pin; clients send an `idempotency_key`.
- Quick filing is one small-model call with the `QuickFiling` schema (below). It sees the note,
  the similar notes' titles and the existing topic list, and returns a title, a kind, topics, an
  urgency and the language. `note_file` stores them and maps urgency to queue priority.
- The answer is delivered twice: as an `answer_user` message as soon as it exists (clients that
  stream the ledger show it immediately) and as `output.response` when the run ends (clients
  that poll the run read it there). `process_inline` is the client's choice: the web app sends
  its "Instant linking" setting (`process_inline_default`, off by default); the watch always
  sends `false` and shows the filing answer.

### note-process

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S[on_flow_start note_id, provider?, model?] --> X[tool note_context<br/>text, extracted attachment text,<br/>similar notes, candidate entities,<br/>recent claims about them, topics]
    X --> P1[code: extraction packet<br/>per section]
    P1 --> E[llm_call extract<br/>resp_schema Extraction]
    E --> R[tool note_resolve_candidates<br/>per mention: alias, full-text, vector candidates]
    R --> P2[code: linking parts<br/>at most 15 mentions each]
    P2 --> J[llm_call link, once per part<br/>resp_schema Linking]
    J --> M[code: merge the parts]
    M --> A[tool note_apply_revision]
    A --> Z[on_flow_end revision summary]
```

1. **Context** (`note_context`): what the notebook already knows that is relevant: the nearest
   notes, entities whose names or aliases appear in the text or whose embeddings are close,
   their current summaries and their most recent active claims, the open tasks that mention
   them, and the topic vocabulary. This is the "look at the existing knowledge" step.
2. **Extract** (`Extraction` schema), once per section: summary, mentions (name, kind, aliases
   seen, role in the note), claims (subject, predicate, object, literal flag, certainty, stance,
   evidence excerpt, optional validity dates), tasks (opened, completed), time references, and
   topics. The model sees the section's whole text and a bounded orientation packet (see
   "Prompts and bounds"); the predicate vocabulary from the AbstractSemantics registry is in the
   static system prompt and `ex:` is allowed for the rest.
3. **Resolve candidates** (`note_resolve_candidates`): for every mention, up to three existing
   entities with their kind, aliases, summary, last seen date, how they matched, and their most
   recent active claims.
4. **Link** (`Linking` schema), once per part of at most 15 mentions: the model decides, per
   mention, `reuse` (a candidate index), `create`, or `merge` (two candidate indexes); per
   claim, whether it `restates` an existing claim (reinforce), `refines` it (new claim, old stays
   active), `supersedes` it (close the old one) or `contradicts` it (both stay, marked disputed),
   naming the existing claim by its `#` index in the packet; per task, open or close by index, quoting
   the note's words that say it is done (`evidence`).
   Each part carries the claims whose subject is one of its mentions (the first part also the
   tasks and the open tasks they may close); claim, task and packet indexes stay those of the
   whole note, so the parts merge back into one Linking without renumbering. The schema uses
   indexes and enumerations rather than free-form ids so that small models cannot invent
   identifiers; `note_apply_revision` rejects any reference outside the packet and downgrades it
   to `create` or `new` with a warning. The model also writes the revision summary and a
   summary for each entity it creates and for each reused entity whose description the note
   changes: what the entity is on the note's date (see "Prompts and bounds"), never an event. A missing summary is never a failed note: a created entity gets one
   built from its role in the note (or where it was seen) and a reused entity keeps its current
   summary, each with a warning in the revision.
5. **Apply** (`note_apply_revision`): checks the decisions structurally, then writes the revision ops to the
   index and the triple store in one transaction per store, updates relations, topics, tasks, embeddings, and
   marks the note `processed`. The checks (data-model.md "Identity and de-duplication" and "Time"): a merge applies
   only with the same kind, a shared name or alias key, fewer than 5 notes on the merged entry and one merge per
   entry per note (else a close match for review); values (numbers, versions, ids, links, tokens, the generic
   words list) are literals, never entities; `supersedes`/`contradicts` only on the same resolved subject and
   predicate; time-aware placement: a note older than the statement it supersedes is inserted before it as the
   earlier belief (`claim.insert_before`), never closing it; a task closes only with the note's own words and never
   from an older note; a stated `document_date` redates a note whose date is approximate (`note.redate`); no window
   ends before it starts. A note older than what is known about an entity marks it (stale summary, then-versus-now
   dropped, `graph_version`) for the consolidation. The response lists created and merged entities, claims added and superseded, and
   any warnings (unknown predicates mapped to `ex:`, unresolved references, missing summaries).

Large notes: `note_context` splits texts beyond the model's budget into sections; `note-process`
loops over sections for extraction and merges mentions and claims before linking, so no text is
ever truncated.

### note-drain and the queue

The queue lives in the note index (`queue` table): `note_id, priority, enqueued_at, leased_by,
lease_until, attempts, last_error`. Ordering is `priority desc, occurred_at asc, size asc`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S[on_flow_start max_items, budget_s, provider?, model?] --> L[tool note_queue_lease worker_id]
    L --> H{item?}
    H -- none --> Z[on_flow_end report]
    H -- yes --> P[subflow note-process]
    P --> K[tool note_queue_ack outcome, error?]
    K --> B{budget left?}
    B -- yes --> L
    B -- no --> Z
```

- A lease lasts 15 minutes. Acknowledging a failure increments `attempts` and schedules a retry
  (after 1 minute, then after 10 minutes); the third failure sets the note to `failed`, visible in
  the web app's queue panel with the error, and offers a manual retry.
- An expired lease (the drain stopped, for example on a gateway restart) is not taken over at once:
  the next drain that leases counts it as a failure ("Processing stopped before it finished.") with
  the same backoff, and a drain retakes the note once that backoff has passed. It counts toward the
  same three failures, so a note whose processing is cut off three times (three restarts during
  the same long note) becomes `failed` and waits for a manual retry.
- **The processor automation.** `POST /api/gateway/note/processor/ensure` (the web app calls it
  when it opens and an automation is missing or unhealthy) creates two automations per user, idempotently: the processor
  (trigger `schedule@2` every `2m`, flow `note-drain`, `max_items = 20`, `budget_s = 90`) and the
  reflect automation (every `7d` by default, flow `note-reflect`), each with
  `_runtime.allowed_tools` listing the note tools. The processor's first drain runs at creation
  (an empty queue completes without a model call); the reflect automation's schedule starts one
  interval after creation (`start_at = now + every`), so opening an empty notebook never starts an
  answering-model call. "Reflect now" is the same `run_now` command sent to the reflect automation
  (`POST /api/gateway/automations/{reflect_id}/commands` with `{"command_id": "<uuid>", "type":
  "automation.run_now"}`).
  Automations run occurrences serially and coalesce missed ticks, which gives the queue exactly
  the eventual, ordered consistency it needs without a gateway worker. "Process now" sends the
  automation's `run_now` command; a `409 automation_busy` answer means a drain is already running
  and the queue panel says so. Steady-state throughput is at most `max_items` per interval.
- **Surviving an upgrade.** An automation runs one concrete workflow version: the gateway resolves
  `bundle_ref: "abstractnote"` to the latest loaded version when the automation is created and
  stores `abstractnote@<version>:note-drain` in its definition, and the runtime starts exactly that
  id at every occurrence. There is no "latest" target (AbstractGateway 0.15.11,
  `routes/automations.py` `_resolve_target`), and the gateway serves only the installed version of
  the note workflows, so after an upgrade and a restart the old automation's next occurrence fails
  ("Workflow 'abstractnote@0.1.0:note-drain' not found in registry") and the queue stops draining. A
  revision of the target cannot fix it either: a failed automation accepts only `archive`.
  The same holds for the tool list: the automation's run input freezes `_runtime.allowed_tools`
  at creation, so a tool added later (`note_communities_recompute` in reflect) is refused at its
  step ("Tool ... is not allowed for this node or run").
  So `processor/ensure` repairs: it keeps an automation that is active or paused on the served
  version with exactly the current tools (`abstractnote.tools.TOOL_NAMES`); any other one (another
  version or tool list, failed, completed, archived, gone) is archived (its
  history stays) and replaced by a new automation built from the current settings
  (`processor_schedule`, `reflect_schedule`, the models), under the next request generation
  (`abstractnote-processor-<n>`) so the replacement is a new automation, never the failed one. A
  paused automation's replacement is paused again (its first tick one interval out, so no drain
  runs before the pause lands). `GET /note/status` and `GET /note/queue` report each automation's
  health (`automations.processor` and `.reflect`: `{id, state, target, healthy, reason, paused}`);
  the web app repairs on load when one is unhealthy, and its queue panel shows "Processor needs
  repair." with a Repair button. Without the note workflows loaded, `ensure` answers 503 and
  archives nothing.
- **No approval waits.** Inside the gateway the note tools are added to the tool approval
  auto-approve set when the runtime is built, so a capture never parks on a tool-approval wait.
- **Priority**: `3` urgent and `2` high come from the quick filing step (tasks with deadlines,
  warnings, anything the user marks urgent); `1` normal is the default for interactive capture;
  `0` bulk is used by importers so that live notes always go first.
- **Concurrency**: one occurrence at a time per user; the gateway's own runner limits concurrent
  ticks across users. Local models serve requests one at a time, so serial processing is also
  the fastest total throughput on a single machine.

### note-recall

`note-recall` also serves the `abstractcode.agent.v1` chat contract: it accepts `prompt` as an
alias of `question` and always returns the answer text on the `response` output pin next to the
structured pins, so a chat client that polls `output.response` shows the answer.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S[on_flow_start question or prompt, effort, as_of?, since?, until?,<br/>entities?, topics?, provider?, model?] --> Q[tool note_search quick]
    Q --> E{effort}
    E -- quick --> Z1[on_flow_end response, hits]
    E -- standard --> X[tool note_expand<br/>entity cards as_of, claims timeline,<br/>neighbours, then-vs-now pairs]
    X --> L[llm_call synthesize<br/>resp_schema Answer]
    L --> Z2[on_flow_end response, answer, evidence, follow_ups]
    E -- deep --> M[subflow note-mine] --> Z3[on_flow_end answer, dossier_note_id]
```

The `Answer` schema returns the answer text with inline citations `[nt_...]`, the evidence list,
what changed over time about the subject (earliest stance, latest stance, turning points with
note ids), open loops related to the question, and suggested follow-up questions. Clients render
citations as links to notes.

### note-mine (deep)

1. `llm_call plan` (`MiningPlan` schema): sub-questions, time slices, entities to trace,
   contradictions to test, a budget of search rounds.
2. Loop over the plan: `note_search` and `note_entity` for each item, `llm_call findings` per
   slice (`SliceFindings` schema: facts with citations, changes, gaps).
3. `llm_call dossier` (`Dossier` schema): narrative, timeline of the subject, how the view evolved,
   contradictions, forgotten items worth revisiting, suggestions, and a confidence statement.
4. `note_insight_write` stores the dossier as a `synthesis` note with provenance (the run id,
   the evidence notes, the entities), so the result is itself searchable and revisitable.

### note-reflect

Runs from a scheduled automation (default weekly, configurable); its first occurrence is one
interval after the automation is created, and "Reflect now" (`automation.run_now`) runs it at once.
A failed occurrence is retried by the automation (up to 3 attempts). Deterministic tools produce
candidates; the model judges and writes:

| Tool | Candidates |
|---|---|
| `note_open_loops` | open tasks last mentioned more than 14 days ago (or revisited at least twice), questions never answered |
| `note_contradictions` | disputed claim pairs only (a note's `contradicts` decision); a subject with several current objects of one predicate is never a candidate, since processing records no single-valued predicates |
| `note_resurface` | entities and topics active before but silent for N days that relate to recent notes |
| `note_anniversaries` | notes from the same day in previous months or years |

`llm_call reflect` (`Reflections` schema) selects what deserves attention and writes each item
as an `insight` note (`warning`, `reminder`, `connection`, `contradiction`, `evolution`). The
web app's Remember view and the watch's Today screen show unacknowledged insights.

A cue is said once until you acknowledge it (`abstractnote.recall.reflect`, data check D5). A
candidate whose provenance (the notes and entities an insight written from it would cite) already backs
an unacknowledged insight is not offered again; `note_insight_write` returns that insight as a
`duplicate` when another of the same kind about the same notes and entities is written, however it is
worded. An age counts from the LAST mention of the subject: a task from its note or the latest note that
revisits it. A date that is only an approximation (`date_basis` `git_added`, `bulk_commit`,
`file_mtime`, `store_updated`, `last_record`, `front_matter_modified`; importers.md "Dates") never ages
anything: such a task or question is not offered as old and is never `stale` (the tasks view too), an
entity or topic whose last mention is so dated is not offered as gone quiet, and such a note has no
anniversary. A run writes at most 3 insights of one kind (`REFLECT_PER_KIND`) and one per candidate.

Then the flow refreshes the communities of the graph and names them (backlog 0030):
`note_communities_recompute` runs Louvain over the entity graph without a model (data-model.md
"Community"); `note_communities_pending` lists up to 5 communities with a stale label or without one
(stale labels first, so every reflect names them again however many new groups wait; then the largest),
each with its top entities, its strongest statements and 3 representative notes; when the list
is empty the run ends there (no model call); otherwise ONE `llm_call` (`CommunityLabels` schema,
thinking off, at most 2048 output tokens) names them all by index, a code node maps each index back to
its community (an index the list does not have is dropped), and `note_communities_label` stores the
names. The run's output adds `communities_labelled` (the number of communities named). The step's
static system prompt and template live in `abstractnote.recall.communities` (`LABEL_SYSTEM_PROMPT`,
`LABEL_TEMPLATE`), next to the schema. `POST /note/communities/recompute` runs detection alone.

The edges detection weighs are the statements between two entities plus their co-mentions: a note
that mentions `k >= 2` live entities adds `1 / ((k - 1) · log2 k)` to every pair among them
(`communities.co_mention_share`). A two-entity note adds 1 to its pair, like one statement; a note's
total co-mention weight is `k / (2 · log2 k)`, so a 200-entity note counts about 13 times a
two-entity note, not 100 times as the flat `1 / (k - 1)` share made it. A single long note therefore
no longer forms a community on its own unless its own statements hold its entities together. On the
operator's notebook at revision 373 (networkx 3.6.1) the change took the communities from 21 to 35,
the loose ends from 2 to 4 and the modularity from 0.606 to 0.667; the two largest communities made
mostly of one note (237 and 232 entities, 87 % and 88 % from it) became one (170 entities, 84 %, the
note whose statements link its 137 own entities) and smaller groups.

### note-consolidate (memory consolidation)

Runs from a third scheduled automation, `consolidate` (backlog 0032; interface
`abstractnote.consolidate.v1`): the `consolidate_schedule` setting gives its interval (`{"every": "1d"}` by
default; `12h`, `7d` and any number of hours or days are accepted; `off` keeps it paused), its first
occurrence is one interval after creation, and "Consolidate now" (`automation.run_now`) runs it at once. It
keeps the notebook's derived memory fresh, in stages, each reporting its progress:

| Stage | What runs | Model |
|---|---|---|
| `normalize` | `note_entities_normalize`: the entries that share a canonical name are merged (`Notebook.normalize_entities`, one reversible revision per merge) | none |
| `communities` | `note_communities_recompute` (as in note-reflect) | none |
| `labels` | loop: `note_communities_pending` (5, `exclude` = the groups skipped this run) -> the reflect naming step (`CommunityLabels`, by index; asked once more when a group is left out) -> `note_communities_label`, until none waits that was not skipped, or the budget is spent | 1 call per 5 groups (2 when the first answer leaves one out) |
| `summaries` | loop: `note_entities_stale_summaries` (8) -> `llm_call summaries` (`EntitySummaries`: `[{index, summary}]`; `summaries_again` when an entry is left out or empty) -> `note_entities_set_summaries`, until none is stale that was not offered this run, or the budget is spent | 1 call per 8 entries (2 when the first answer leaves one out) |
| `then_now` | `note_then_now_refresh`: the then-versus-now cache of every entry this run merged into or summarised | none |
| `reflect` | the note-reflect flow as a subflow (open loops, tensions, resurfacing, anniversaries -> insights; its naming finds nothing left) | as note-reflect |

A summary is stale when it is empty, when it is still the placeholder an entry was created with (the
revision builder recorded "No summary was written for <name>; it was described from this note." and no
summary was written since), or when a note mention or a statement about the entry (or an entry merged into
it) was recorded by a revision after its latest summary's revision. Nothing reads the summary's wording
(ADR 0004). Each entry handed to the model carries its name, kind, other names, current summary, its
strongest statements in words (at most 8) and its 3 newest note excerpts; the prompt
(`process/prompts/entity_summaries`) asks for at most two sentences, third person, present tense, nothing
the statements and notes do not say. The answers are mapped back by index. Nothing stops or is left out
silently (ADR 0007, the incident of 2026-10-20 where one empty answer ended the stage as "completed" with 536
summaries stale): a round whose answer leaves out an offered entry or group (or answers it empty) asks once
more with the same prompt; what is still unanswered is skipped for this run (reported with the round's
`note_consolidation_progress(..., skipped, reason)`, logged on `abstractnote.consolidation`, recorded on the
stage) and never offered again in the run, and the loop goes on. A summary over 600 characters or a label over
4 words is kept whole with an `over_length` warning. At the close, `note_consolidation_end` reports `left_out =
{summaries, labels, reasons}` (the skipped items still pending, plus what the budget did not reach:
`budget_spent`, `not_reached`) and closes the run as `completed_with_gaps` when anything was left out; the
run's answer then reads "Consolidated with gaps: …" followed by the end-user notice ("12 summaries could not be
refreshed this time; they will be tried again next time."). Each round's summaries are one revision (`action: entity.summary`,
`run_id` = the consolidation id, source client `consolidation`), so the summary history keeps every version
and a rebuild replays it.

The start pins are `budget_s` (default 3600: the loops stop starting rounds after it), `limit` (the reflect
stage's insight limit, default 10), `thinking` (`on` or `off`, default `off`, wired to both model steps) and
the model pins. Progress: the flow calls `note_consolidation_begin` (an earlier row still open is closed as
`interrupted`), then `note_consolidation_progress(stage, done, total, skipped?, reason?)` at the start and
after each step of every stage, then `note_consolidation_end(status, results)`. The rows live in the notebook's
`consolidation_runs` table (kept by a rebuild); a stage's seconds per item are measured from its first
report, and its ETA is the items it has left times that measure (the last completed run's measure for the
stage until one item is done). After `begin` no tool step raises: a failed step's sentence is remembered and
one failure path closes the consolidation as `failed` and ends the run with that sentence (inside a loop a
raising node would only end the round); a node that breaks inside a round leaves the round's in-flight flag
set and the check after the loop fails the run the same way. A model call that fails ends the run at once;
its row stays open and reads as `interrupted` (`GET /note/consolidation` once the automation's run has
ended, and the next `begin`).

## Structured output schemas

All schemas are JSON Schema objects attached as `resp_schema`; the runtime builds pydantic
models from them and repairs invalid output. Python mirrors live in `abstractnote.process.schemas`.

**QuickFiling**

```json
{"title": "string (<= 80 chars)", "kind": "idea|task|decision|fact|event|question|reflection|reference|log|conversation|personal",
 "topics": ["string, prefer existing topics, at most 4"], "urgency": "bulk|normal|high|urgent",
 "language": "BCP-47", "one_line": "string"}
```

**Extraction**

```json
{"summary": "1-3 sentences",
 "mentions": [{"ref": "m1", "name": "string", "kind": "person|org|project|concept|place|event|artifact|software|thing",
               "aliases": ["as written in the note"], "role": "what the note says about it, one phrase"}],
 "claims": [{"subject": "m1", "predicate": "CURIE from the vocabulary or ex:snake_case", "object": "m2 or literal",
             "object_is_literal": false, "certainty": "stated|probable|possible|reported|disputed",
             "stance": "assert|revise|retract", "evidence": "verbatim excerpt", "valid_from": "ISO or null", "valid_until": "ISO or null"}],
 "tasks": [{"text": "string", "status": "open|done", "due": "ISO or null"}],
 "time_refs": [{"text": "string", "iso": "ISO or null"}],
 "topics": ["string"],
 "document_date": {"iso": "ISO date", "basis": "stated in the text", "quote": "the exact words"} or null}
```

Fields with a default may be left out by the model (the runtime fills the default): in
Extraction `aliases` ([]), `object_is_literal` (false), `certainty` (stated), `stance` (assert),
`valid_from`, `valid_until`, `due`, `iso` and `document_date` (null; given only when the header says the note's
date is approximate and the text states its own date); in Linking `candidate` (null),
`merge_candidates` ([]), `name` (""), `kind` (null), `aliases` ([]), `reason` (""), `existing`
(null), `closes_open_task` (null) and `evidence` ("": a close without it is not applied). `claims` lists only the statements that relate to an
existing one (a statement left out is `new`) and `tasks` only those that close an open task.

**Linking** (indexes refer to the candidate lists in the context packet; enumerations are JSON
Schema enums)

```json
{"mentions": [{"ref": "m1", "decision": "reuse|create|merge|unsure", "candidate": 0,
               "merge_candidates": [0, 1], "name": "preferred name", "kind": "person|org|project|concept|place|event|artifact|software|thing",
               "aliases": ["..."], "summary": "what the entity is on the note's date, one or two sentences: for create and unsure, and for a reused entity whose description this note changes; otherwise null (a missing one is a warning, never a failed note)", "reason": "short"}],
 "claims": [{"index": 0, "relation_to_existing": "new|restates|refines|supersedes|contradicts",
             "existing": 0, "reason": "short"}],
 "tasks": [{"index": 0, "closes_open_task": 0, "evidence": "the note's words that say it is done"}],
 "revision_summary": "one sentence"}
```
