
**Answer**, **MiningPlan**, **SliceFindings**, **Dossier**, **Reflections**: see
`abstractnote.process.schemas`; each is documented inline with the fields listed above.

**CommunityLabels** (the reflect flow's naming step; defined in `abstractnote.recall.communities`
and merged into the flow schemas by `flows.build.load_schemas`)

```json
{"communities": [{"index": 0, "label": "at most 4 words", "summary": "one sentence",
                  "kind": "project|theme|people|tooling|process|other"}]}
```

**EntitySummaries** (the consolidation's summary step; `process.schemas.ENTITY_SUMMARIES`, merged into the
flow schemas by `flows.build.flow_schemas`)

```json
{"summaries": [{"index": 0, "summary": "at most two sentences, third person, present tense"}]}
```

## Prompts and bounds

Every model step has two Markdown files under `src/abstractnote/process/prompts/`:

- `<step>.system.md`, the **static system prompt**: the instructions, the output shape with one
  illustrative answer, and the rules; the extraction one also lists the predicate vocabulary
  from the AbstractSemantics registry with one-line glosses, filled in when the flows are
  generated. These bytes are the same for every note, so a local model's prompt cache reuses
  them (below).
- `<step>.md`, the **dynamic user message**: rendered inside the flow by a `string_template`
  node from a packet that a code node builds with `abstractnote.process.packets` (the flows'
  code nodes carry that module's own source, so Python and the flows cannot drift).

The note steps' user message starts with one constant envelope,
`<runtime_metadata>{"time": "the note's own date is on the last line of this message"}</runtime_metadata>`,
and ends with a line that identifies the note: `About this note (not part of its text): nt_…
“title”, written 2026-07-10 08:47 (now, for this note) (kind …; from …) [part 2 of 3]`. The
runtime keeps an envelope already at the head of a message byte for byte (it stamps a fresh
per-second one on a message without one), so no per-call value sits in the shared prefix; the
note's date is "now" for the model (relative dates resolve from it) and the system prompt says
the last line is not content. The user templates end without trailing whitespace, which the
runtime needs to recognise the envelope as the message's own.

A prompt note from the Claude sessions importer keeps the assistant's answer in
`source.origin.outcome` by `source.origin.outcome_author` (and appended to the text):
`note_context` then returns the author's text and the answer as separate sections (`source`
`note` or `answer`, with their `author`), and the packet labels them "Text written by …" and
"Answer by … (what they said; not written by the note's author)"; the extraction prompt
writes statements from an answer as `reported`.

Rules that every prompt states:

- Use only the note and the provided context; never invent entities or dates.
- Prefer reusing an existing entity when the candidate list contains it; create sparingly.
- Keep names as written by the author; put variants in aliases.
- Quote evidence verbatim; one claim per statement; no inferred hierarchy.
- When unsure whether two things are the same, say `unsure` (treated as `create` plus a
  `skos:closeMatch` claim for later consolidation) rather than guessing.
- Output JSON only, matching the schema.

Predicates outside the vocabulary are accepted as `ex:snake_case` and reported in the revision
warnings so the vocabulary can grow deliberately.

**Kinds: seats are not packages (eval2 D7).** The eval2 corpus folded agora seats (`gateway`, `core`,
the agents that write the messages) into the packages they own (`abstractgateway`, `abstractcore`). The
extraction and linking prompts carry one glossary line for the nine kinds (a person is a human, or an
AI agent or seat that writes, decides or acts; software is a program, package, library, service or
tool; ...); extraction gives two mentions with two kinds when one name means both in the text; the
linking packet shows every mention and candidate as `name — kind`, and the prompt says to compare kinds
as well as names (a person is never the software, project or artifact it owns or works on) and, when
a candidate has the very same name but is a different thing, to create the new entity under a name
that tells them apart as the text would say it (`gateway seat`) with the shared name as an alias (an
entity of the same canonical name would otherwise be the same entity, data-model.md "Entity").

**Choosing a predicate (eval2 D6).** The eval2 notebook's claims collapsed onto a few generic
predicates (`schema:mentions` 32 %, `schema:participant` 10 %, `schema:name` 8 %, `schema:nextItem` 5 %),
so a later value rarely met the earlier one on the same predicate. The extraction prompt therefore
says how to choose one, with examples and no closed list (the model decides): the relation the text
states, read from the subject to the object (`X ex:depends_on Y`), never backwards; a CURIE only when
its meaning is exactly that relation (`schema:participant` is taking part in an event or a project,
`schema:nextItem` the next item of a sequence, names go in aliases); otherwise a specific `ex:` verb
or attribute (`ex:maintains`, `ex:runs_on`, `ex:fixed_in`, `ex:status`, `ex:version`, ...); never a
vague one when the text says how two things relate; a fact with one value at a time (status, version,
owner, deadline, place) always takes the same predicate, while a relation that adds up is one statement
per value. The extraction packet lists the predicates the notebook already uses about the names it
shows (`packets.KNOWN_PREDICATES`), and the prompt asks to reuse them for the same relation, so a new
status supersedes the old one on the same subject and predicate (the apply check).

**Bounds.** Only the packet is bounded; the note's text is never cut (long notes are split into
sections, each read whole).

| Packet | Bound (`abstractnote.process.packets`) |
|---|---|
| Extraction orientation | names and kinds of at most 15 known entities (no claims), the predicates of their current statements (at most 15, the most used first; `schema:mentions` never), at most 50 topics (the note's own first, then the most used), 5 similar notes by title and date, 8 open tasks, one line each |
| Candidates per mention | 3 (`note_resolve_candidates`) |
| Candidate card | name, kind, up to 5 aliases, summary (at most 240 characters; `[LATER]` when it was written on a later day than the note), last seen, and at most 3 active claims as one line each, those with a predicate the note also uses first (`LATER than this note` when first seen on a later day) |
| Mentions per linking call | 15; the rest go to further calls for the same note, merged back |
| Statement lines | subject, predicate, object, certainty, stance, evidence (at most 200 characters) |
| Open tasks in linking | only when the note has tasks, at most 8 |
| Section | 6000 characters per extraction call (`note_context` `max_chars`), so each answer fits the extract output cap |

**Checks on the answers.** A section of at least 200 characters whose extraction names nothing is
read once more; a second empty answer is kept and the revision says so ("A part of this note
names nothing although it has text, even when read a second time."). `note_apply_revision`
leaves out, with a warning, a mention whose name and aliases never occur as whole words in the
note's own text (its title and header do not count: names copied from the context packet are
refused); a statement about it is skipped, one pointing at it keeps the name as text. A reused
entity gains only the aliases the linking lists for it, and `unsure` without a candidate is
created as new with a warning. The prompts also state: reuse an entity only when the mention
names that very thing (a part, version, file or tool of X is a new entity related to X); one to
three topics; no statement whose only content is that the text mentions something (`schema:mentions`, `ex:mentions` or any other word for it), and
`dcterms:hasPart` only when stated; proposals and plans are `possible`; a superseded statement
is written with `stance: retract` and its end date, the replacing one with `stance: revise`.

**Entity summaries (eval2 D4).** A summary says what the entity IS on the note's date: its kind,
its role or what it is for, and who or what it belongs to, works with or is part of; only a fact
that can change (a status, an owner, a version, a role) carries its date ("since 2026-10"); one or two sentences, at most about 240 characters
(the card's clip, so a summary is always shown whole; the consolidation leaves out one over 600). It
is never a sentence about the note or one event ("Dana confirmed the schedule"): the linking
rewrites a reused entity's summary only when the note changes what it is, folding the new fact into
the current description, and answers null when the entity only did something (that is a statement).
The candidate card marks a summary written on a later day than the note `[LATER]` and such statements
`LATER than this note` (`context.summary_at`, the history date of the current summary); the prompt
says to use them only to recognise the entity, so an earlier note describes the entity from itself
and the earlier statements (its summary is stored at its own date; the latest stays current). The
consolidation's summary prompt asks for the same description in the present tense.

## Prompt cache, thinking and output caps

**Prompt cache.** It applies only on AbstractCore's prompted structured-output lane; on the
Outlines lane (below), which the gateway and the headless runner use for MLX today, no call
uses or reports a prompt cache. On the prompted lane AbstractRuntime derives one prompt-cache
key per (session, provider, model, flow, node) for every run that has a session, so all notes
processed in one session share one key per step (the processor automation has a session). Hybrid models
such as Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Gated-DeltaNet plus attention) restore only an exactly stored prefix:
after each call the provider snapshots the part of the prompt that the last two calls on the
key shared, and the next call reuses it when its prompt extends that snapshot. Every note
step's prompt is the same system prompt followed by the same envelope, with the note's id and
date on the last line, so consecutive notes share at least the whole system prompt. When two
consecutive notes also share the first words of their text, the snapshot moves past the system
prompt and a following note that starts differently cannot extend it: that call is a full
prefill ("rebuilt"), and the next one hits again (backlog 0024 measures how often). (A fresh key would fork
the runtime's prepared system prefix instead, but for chat templates that render tool
definitions before the system text, as Qwen3.5 and 3.6 do, that prefix is 3 tokens long; the
flows therefore do not give each note its own cache scope.) The provider reports each call's
`prompt_cache` record (`outcome`, `cached_tokens`, `fed_tokens`); AbstractRuntime does not copy
it into the ledger for structured calls today (a structured result carries no metadata), so
backlog 0024's measurements read it at the provider.

**Structured output lane.** With Outlines installed, AbstractCore's MLX and HuggingFace providers
decode structured output through Outlines unless `structured_output_method="prompted"`. That lane
bypasses the prompt cache, cannot think, and applies the chat template a second time around the
already rendered prompt; the system prompts therefore carry the output shape, so the model
writes the right fields on either lane (on the old prompts, with thinking off, this lane
answered empty lists). A provider created with `structured_output_method="prompted"` (for
example `NoteRunner.local(..., llm_kwargs={"structured_output_method": "prompted"})`) generates
normally and uses the prompt cache, but with thinking on it reasons for minutes per call
(backlog 0024 measured 160-181 s per extraction), so the flows do not ask for it.

**Thinking and output caps** are pinned on each `llm_call` node (a node value wins over the run's
`_runtime.thinking`):

| Step | Thinking | Output cap (tokens) |
|---|---|---|
| quick filing | off | 400 |
| extract (and its second reading) | on (`thinking` start pin; `off` from note-drain) | 4000 |
| link | on (`thinking` start pin; `off` from note-drain) | 6000 |
| synthesize, dossier, reflect | the runtime default | 8192 |
| mining plan, slice findings | the runtime default | 4096 |
| naming communities (reflect) | off | 2048 |
| naming communities, entity summaries (note-consolidate) | `thinking` start pin, default off | 2048, 3000 |

Thinking for extraction and linking is a per-run choice: `note-process` takes a `thinking`
start pin (`on` or `off`, default `on`, anything else is refused) wired to the extract, second
reading and link nodes; `note-drain` takes its own `thinking` pin, default `off` (the bulk-import
setting: a thinking call can run to its output budget and AbstractCore then retries with a
larger one, measured 114-352 s for one section on the live drain), and passes it to every
`note-process` it starts; inline processing at capture keeps `on`. The table above gives the
defaults.

On MLX, Qwen3.6 has only an on/off switch (`enable_thinking`): any level ("low", "medium") is
treated as on and there is no thinking budget, so a thinking step can run until the output cap.
On the Outlines lane "on" changes only how the prompt ends (JSON-constrained decoding leaves no
room to reason); a failed Outlines decode falls back to normal generation, which then does think.
A truncated structured answer is retried by AbstractCore's structured-output handler with a
doubled budget, at most three attempts; a flow cannot turn that off today, so the caps are set
well above what a bounded section or linking part needs.

## Headless execution

`abstractnote process --local --notebook DIR --provider mlx --model <id>` runs `note-drain` without a gateway:
the same compiled flows on a local `Runtime` with real effect handlers (AbstractCore model calls,
the note tools bound to a local notebook directory). This is how the importers are processed in
bulk, how the test suite exercises the flows with a scripted model, and how you can run the
processor on a machine that is not the gateway host. The recipe follows AbstractRuntime's
`test_kg_learn_and_recall_contract` harness (`compile_visualflow_tree`, `WorkflowRegistry`,
`build_effect_handlers`, drive subflow waits).

---

## docs/remembering.md

# Remembering

Search engines answer queries. Memory answers cues. AbstractNote's recall is built around the
ways people (and agents) actually try to remember, and around how much effort they are willing
to spend. This page explains the design that the **Remember** view, the recall tools and the
`note-recall` flow implement.

## How we remember

| Cue | What you have | What you want | AbstractNote answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time | "around the release in September", "last winter" | what was going on then | the day and period views: notes, revisions, entities touched, what you believed then |
| Person or thing | "Dana", "the LUT project" | everything you know, and how it changed | the entity card as of a moment, the claims timeline, then-versus-now |
| Fragment | three words you are sure were in the note | the note | quick recall: full-text plus vector, the entities and statements grouped under the notes that carry them, each entity with its first and latest date |
| First mention | "when did we first talk about X?" | the oldest note | quick recall in earliest order: the notes that match X, oldest first |
| Feeling or shape | "that idea I was excited about", "a warning I wrote myself" | the note or the insight | kinds and topics as filters, insights as first-class notes |
| Association | "it came up together with X" | the neighbours | graph expansion from the hits, relations with first and last seen |
| Absence | "did I ever decide this?" "what have I dropped?" | the gap | open loops, contradictions, resurfacing, the reflect insights |
| Evolution | "what did I used to think?" | the arc | earliest stance, latest stance, turning points with the notes that caused them |

Agents have the same needs with different vocabulary: an agent asked to continue work needs the
latest decision and the reason it changed; an agent starting a task needs the entities involved
and their current state; an agent writing a report needs the timeline with citations. The same
structures serve both, which is why every answer is returned as structured JSON with note ids as
citations, and the web app renders that JSON.

## Effort levels

| Level | Budget | What runs | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| **quick** | under a second, no model | full-text (FTS5, BM25) plus vector search over notes, entities and claims, with a relevance floor; entities and statements grouped under the notes that carry them; relevance or earliest order; facets | hits with excerpts, matched entities with their first and latest date, matched claims, facets |
| **standard** | seconds, one model call | quick retrieval, then a recall packet chosen within a budget (24,000 characters by default): the best notes with excerpts around the matches, entity cards as of the requested moment as one line each, and for the entities the question is about their claim timelines, neighbours and then-versus-now pairs; then one synthesis | an answer with citations, the evidence, the evolution summary, open loops, follow-ups |
| **deep** | minutes, several model calls, runs in the background | a mining plan (sub-questions, time slices, entities, contradictions), several retrieval rounds with findings per slice, a dossier | the dossier as an answer and as a stored `synthesis` note; the web app and the watch show it when it is ready |

The level is a parameter everywhere: the Remember view has an effort dial, the watch asks at
standard by default, agents pass it explicitly, and the CLI takes `--effort`. A deep search is
never blocking: the run starts, the client gets a run id, and the dossier appears as an insight.

### Quick relevance

Ranking fuses full-text and vector ranks, which orders hits but cannot tell a good hit from the best
of a bad lot. So every hit also gets a relevance from 0 to 1: the share of the question's words it
contains, each word weighted by how rare it is among your notes (the square of its inverse document
frequency, so "Tailscale" counts far more than "when" or "first"; a word no note contains counts for
nothing), raised but never lowered by the vector similarity. An entity or a statement is shown only
when its relevance reaches 0.5 and one of the returned notes carries it (the note mentions the
entity, or made or repeated the statement); it is shown under those notes, and an entity with the
first and the latest date among the matching notes that carry it. Earliest order (`order=earliest`)
lists the notes whose relevance reaches 0.75 oldest first: search for the subject ("Tailscale
HTTPS") to answer "when did we first mention it". The thresholds are `HIT_MIN_SCORE` and
`EARLIEST_MIN_SCORE` in `abstractnote.recall.search`.

## The Remember view

The Remember view opens on what changed and lets you dig from there. Its first screen (since you
last looked beside the cue cards, then the ask bar) fits a 1280x800 window; the rest follows below.

1. **Since you last looked** (the default screen): what the notebook learned since your last
   visit: new entities, beliefs that were replaced ("Replaced") or withdrawn ("Withdrawn"), loops
   that closed, insights, notes that failed to process. It is a system-time delta from a cursor, so it is the same call an agent
   makes at the start of every session (`GET /note/changes?since=`). Each item opens its subject.
   The web app shows it as a compact list, one line per change with a word for its kind
   (Replaced, Withdrawn, Closed, Needs attention, New); new notes fold into one line that opens.
2. **Cue cards**: a few prompts the reflect flow generated from the graph, each answerable by
   adding a note: a person who went quiet, a decision that is a year old, a task mentioned three
   times and never closed. Answering a cue writes a note linked to its subject; the answered
   rate is the measure of whether the cards are worth showing. Cue cards are insights, so an
   insight shown as a cue is not repeated under Revisit or in the delta. Every cue and insight has
   **Why this surfaced**: its kind in plain words (a reminder, a connection, a contradiction, an
   evolution, ...) and the notes it is based on.
3. **The ask bar** with the effort dial and cue chips: *when* (a date, a range, "around" an
   entity's active period), *who/what* (entities), *kind* (idea, decision, task, ...), *topic*.
   Typing shows quick results immediately; with Quick chosen there is no Ask button, the
   matching notes follow the typing. Ask runs standard or deep and shows its steps as they happen
   (searched your notes, looked closer at what they connect, wrote the answer). An answer has three
   layers, each named and drawn differently: the **Synthesis** (what the selected notes suggest,
   with citations), the **Original** (the notes it rests on, quoted as you wrote them) and the
   **Interpretation** (what the notebook understood: how it changed, what is still open). Each
   citation opens the note with its attachments and the revision it caused. "Save this answer"
   turns it into a note with provenance; the note dialog shows such notes as synthesis, never as
   something you wrote.
4. **Then versus now**: for an entity or for a relationship between two entities, the earliest
   and the latest summary side by side, with the turning points between them listed with their
   notes. Cached per revision; the fastest way to see how your understanding of a person, a
   project, an idea or a link evolved.
5. **Why do I believe this**: every claim, and every sentence of an answer, opens its evidence
   chain: the claim, what it superseded or was superseded by, the notes, the attachment excerpt.
   One tap says "this is wrong" and writes a retract revision with your account as the source.
6. **Revisit**: open loops with a close action and their age (an open loop still open after 60
   days is marked stale, so it can be closed or left to age out), unread insights, "on this day" notes, entities
   that went silent but relate to what you added this week, contradictions awaiting a decision.
7. **To review** (only when there is something, `GET /note/review`): what the notebook decided
   on its own, each with why, the two sides, the notes behind them and its own actions. A merge it
   made: **Keep** (recorded for your account, `POST /note/review/{id}/confirm`) or **Undo the
   match** (separates them again; the joined entry's own name and notes come from
   `GET /note/entities/{id}?as_merged=true`). A close match it was unsure about: **Same** (joins
   them) or **Not the same** (withdraws the close match). Two notes that disagree: say which one is
   wrong (withdraws that statement).

Each entity card carries a small activity sparkline. A multi-lane time river is a candidate for
a later version once real notebooks show which lanes deserve a lane; the time scrubber in the
Explore view already covers "what did this look like then".

## The Explore view (the graph)

- **Focus and depth**: pick one or several entities; see their neighbourhood up to depth three,
  edges labelled by predicate with first and last seen dates and counts.
- **The picture**: it fits the view when it loads and when its data changes; scroll or pinch to zoom
  about the pointer, drag the background to pan, drag a node to move it (the others settle around it),
  double-click the background or press Fit to view to fit again. Keyboard focus draws a ring around
  the node.
- **Picture or List**: the same connections drawn, or as a readable table (from, link, to, since,
  believed or no longer believed); each row opens the link's history or the entity.
- **Time scrubber and date field**: moving the slider or choosing a date changes `as_of` (the date
  field reaches any day without dragging). Beside it, **True then** reads the date as what your
  notes said was true then (`at`); **Saved by then** reads it as what the notebook held on that
  date (`as_received`: only notes received by then), so a June note imported in October is absent
  from a September snapshot. The layout stays where it is: entities and edges that did not exist yet fade
  out, superseded claims show as dashed; the entity card shows the beliefs at that moment. An edge
  opens the relation timeline between its two entities.
- **Day page**: "what happened on day X": notes captured, revisions applied with their one-line
  summaries, entities created or merged, claims superseded.
- **Entity page** (the topic portrait): name, aliases and activity, then five tabs. **How it
  evolved** comes first: the first note, the dated views from the summary history (earlier view,
  refined, latest expressed view) and the changes between them (a belief replaced or withdrawn),
  oldest first, each opening its note or its evidence; with a date chosen, the milestones after it
  stay in place, faded. Then **Changes** (what you believe or believed then, then-versus-now),
  **Open actions**, **Sources** (the notes) and **Links** (relations). An entity that absorbed
  others names them ("Includes Dana R. (1 note)", from each entry's own record). An entity asked
  for at a date before it existed says so.

## The Capture view

A stream of your notes as you wrote them, with the composer at the bottom. You type or paste,
attach files (images show a preview), drop images, or dictate; Enter saves and Shift+Enter starts
a new line; with your permission the browser attaches your location. Under each note one short
acknowledgement shows one state at a time, as a word and a symbol: **Sending**, **Received**,
**Organizing**, then **Organized** or **Needs attention**. Once organized, the note's title and the
entities it links to come first, with the line "Organized · Added to #lut · event · 2 links" under
them; it opens on what was filed: the note's title, topics, linked entities, when you
said the same thing before, and what it changed. Until the note is organized the details show
the notebook's reply. With "Instant linking" on (Settings) the note is processed right away;
otherwise the app re-reads the note until it is. Nothing uses system vocabulary: no run ids, no
ledger, no gateway.

## The Processing view

Remembering has a cost in time, and the Processing view shows it honestly: what the notebook is
doing with your notes right now, how fast, what is waiting and what went wrong, without system
vocabulary. It also owns the consolidation: the scheduled pass that joins duplicate entries,
recomputes the themes and names the new or stale ones, refreshes entity summaries that are older
than what is known about them, refreshes then-and-now, and looks back for insights. Each stage
reports n of m with a time left measured from its own pace, and "Consolidate now" runs it at
once (see [cognition.md](cognition.md), "note-consolidate"). When a pass could not refresh
everything (the model gave no answer for some entries, or its time ran out), it says so in one
quiet line under the last pass ("12 summaries could not be refreshed this time; they will be tried
again next time.") and the state line reads "Consolidated with gaps"; the next pass tries them
again. Nothing is left out without a word (ADR 0007).

## For agents and entities

- `note_changes` (since you last looked) is the first call of a session; `note_search` at quick
  effort is cheap enough to call before every task.
- `note-recall` at standard effort returns the latest decision and why it changed, with
  citations, in one call; agents should quote the note ids in their own outputs so provenance
  survives.
- Deep recall returns a dossier note id; an agent can wait for the run or come back later.
- Agents capture notes through the same `note-capture` flow with `source.client = "agent"` and
  `source.author = <agent name>`, so the notebook records who learned what and when.

---

## docs/clients.md

# Clients

AbstractNote ships a web app and an Apple Watch app, and reserves the structure for an iPhone
app. All clients are thin: the gateway owns authentication, execution and state. They share one
contract: sign in to a gateway, start the `note-capture` and `note-recall` flows with the runs
API, read the note API for views, and never send user, tenant or runtime identifiers.

## Sign-in and isolation

- A client signs in with a gateway account token (`Authorization: Bearer`) verified against
  `GET /api/gateway/me`, or with an emailed one-time code (`POST /session/recovery/request`, then
  `/redeem`) that yields a session id and CSRF token sent as headers on later requests.
- Sign-out clears the stored credential locally and, for sessions, calls
  `POST /session/logout`. A `401` on any call returns the client to sign-in.
- The gateway routes every request to the caller's own data plane, so one gateway serves many
  users and each sees only their own notebook. Use a dedicated `user`-role account per person or
  device; never an admin token.
- Credential storage on Apple clients: a file in the app container protected with Data
  Protection (`completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication`), not the OS keychain, following the
  framework's file-sealed secrets rule. The gateway address is stored next to it. This choice is
  proposed and awaits a ruling ([ADR 0006](adr/0006-apple-client-credential-storage.md)).

## Web app (`web/`)

- npm package `@abstractframework/note`, built with Vite, React and TypeScript, using
  `@abstractframework/ui-kit`, `@abstractframework/panel-chat` and `@abstractframework/app-server`
  from the npm registry with semver ranges.
- Served by the gateway at `/apps/note/` through the app proxy. The app's Node server answers the
  mount header, relays `/api/*` to the gateway with the session cookie, binds `127.0.0.1`, and
  uses relative URLs and the shared shell, as the app-server contract requires.
- Four views, in the tab order **Capture**, **Remember**, **Explore** (the graph; its route stays
  `#/graph`) and **Processing** (see [remembering.md](remembering.md)), plus a small **Settings**
  drawer (filing model, answering model, inline processing, reflect and consolidation schedules,
  location, queue status with retry, manage connection).
- **Processing** shows, on one screen that never scrolls as a page, what the notebook is doing with
  your notes: one sentence with a live dot (understanding at a pace with the time left, paused,
  stopped and needing a repair, consolidating, or up to date) with Process now, the Automatic
  understanding switch, Repair and Reflect now; the notes being understood right now with their
  step (Reading, Extracting, Linking, Applying) and a Cancel with inline confirmation; the
  consolidation with its stages, "Summaries · 72 of 140", time left, last run, what is waiting,
  Consolidate now and its schedule (12 h, 1 d, 7 d, off); the pace over the last two hours and the
  queue by priority with "Move to front"; the notes just understood; and what needs attention
  (failed notes with Retry, helpers needing a repair). It re-reads `GET /note/processing` three
  seconds after each answer with `If-None-Match`, pauses while the tab is hidden, and keeps the
  last answer on a failure. On phones the sections become a pill row, one at a time. Location is off until you turn on the
  Location switch in Settings (kept per browser, and offered only on a secure page); Capture then
  attaches it to notes.
- Sign-in and the top-right corner are the framework's (ui-kit): `useGatewayConnection` with the
  kit's sign-in card (`GatewaySessionSignInCard`: gateway URL, account, token, keep this browser
  signed in; the app server exchanges the token for an HTTP-only session that survives reloads). The
  address defaults to the app server's own `--gateway-url` (given to the page by `bin/server.js`);
  the last address and account are remembered per browser (the address only while the server still
  points there); a refused sign-in reads as one sentence, and `AfTopBarActions` (appearance, About, Settings,
  the signed-in account, and the Connect / Disconnect pill), and an empty notebook invites the first
  note or `abstractnote import`. At start the app asks
  `GET /note/status`: a 401 opens the sign-in dialog; a 404 while `GET /me` answers shows "AbstractNote
  is not installed on this gateway." instead of the views.
- Theming uses ui-kit tokens only, so every kit theme works; tested on default-dark, observer-night
  and solarized-light at 1280 and 400 px. The framework look comes from derivations of those
  tokens: on dark themes the page colour is deepened toward near-black (relative colour of
  `--bg-primary`; light themes keep theirs), fine borders, Inter when installed (else the kit
  font), and an indigo, cyan and mint accent mixed from `--info`, `--accent` and `--success` used
  for state and emphasis only. Primary actions keep the theme's `--accent`.
- Accessibility: text follows the appearance text size (`--font-scale`, graph labels included);
  focus rings are always visible; every state is a word and a symbol, never colour alone (capture
  states, believed / no longer believed, the answer's three layers); every graph has a readable
  relationship list (Explore, List); dates are chosen with a date field, never only by dragging;
  reduced motion turns animation off.
- Registered by the AbstractGateway integration in the gateway's app catalog, tray, web console
  and terminal console as `note` (port 3006, cookie prefix `abstractnote`, page title
  `AbstractNote`, command `abstractnote-web`).

Development: `npm install`, then `npm run dev -- --gateway-url <url>` serves the app against a
gateway, and `npm run dev:mock` against a built-in sample notebook; `npm run build` produces
`dist/`; `node bin/cli.js --port 3006 --gateway-url
http://127.0.0.1:8080` runs the production server the way the gateway launches it.

## Apple Watch app (`watch/apple/`)

- XcodeGen project `project.yml`: target `AbstractNoteWatch` (watchOS 26, bundle id
  `ai.abstractframework.note.watch`), an empty iOS container `AbstractNote`
  (`ai.abstractframework.note`) for App Store packaging, a UI test target, Swift 6 with strict
  concurrency. `WKWatchOnly` is set; the app runs independently of a phone.
- Swift package `Packages/AbstractGatewayClient`: the gateway client (credential, sign-in,
  requests with read retries, run start and polling, note API reads) and a
  mock client for previews and screenshots. It starts as a documented snapshot of the
  AbstractAssistant watch client (`SNAPSHOT.json` records the source and hashes) and adds the
  note endpoints; the two clients are candidates for a shared package once their APIs settle.
- Screens:
  - **Note**: a text field (watchOS dictation and scribble come free with it) and a Send button at
    the bottom; after sending, the filing answer ("Saved as idea 'LUT budget'. Related: Dana,
    LUT.") with a Done button. Location is attached when the user allowed it. Each send carries a
    fresh idempotency key so a radio retry never duplicates a note.
  - **Ask**: dictate a question, see the standard-effort answer with the evidence titles; "Dig
    deeper" starts a deep recall and the result shows in Today when ready.
  - **Today**: what changed since you last looked, unacknowledged insights, open loops, cue
    cards and on-this-day notes; tap to acknowledge, close, or add a note about it.
  - **Settings**: the server and account, the Place switch (location), About, Sign out.
- Build and test: `scripts/build.sh` (XcodeGen, `swift test`, simulator build, screenshots of
  every screen with the mock client), `scripts/deploy-watch.sh` (signed build and install on a
  paired watch through `devicectl`, gateway and token passed as launch arguments), and a GitHub
  workflow (`.github/workflows/watch.yml`) that builds and tests on every change to `watch/apple/`.
- End-user copy rules: plain verbs, one-sentence errors, actions at the bottom, no system
  vocabulary, VoiceOver labels on every control, no state shown by colour alone, nothing
  consequential without a tap.

## iPhone app (`phone/iphone/`)

Planned. The folder holds the plan: the same package layout as the watch with a richer Capture
(camera, files, voice memos), the full Explore and Remember views, and share-sheet capture from
other apps. The bundle id reserved is `ai.abstractframework.note.iphone`, following the
AbstractAssistant precedent of watch-only plus separate iPhone app; if the watch app should
later become a companion of the iPhone app, the bundle parentage changes before the first
public release of either.

## CLI and agents

The `abstractnote` CLI is a headless tool on a notebook directory (`--notebook DIR`);
`--gateway URL --token T` is reserved for a client mode that is not available in this version.
Agents and entities running inside the same gateway call the note tools directly; agents
elsewhere use the runs API like any client.

## docs/importers.md

# Importers

Importers turn existing corpora into notes with faithful history time and provenance. They write
notes directly into a notebook at bulk priority (`0`) and let the processor understand them in
the background, so a large import never delays live notes. Every imported note keeps a `source`
object that points back to the exact origin, and re-running an import is idempotent because note
ids derive from the source key.

| Importer | Command | One note per | `occurred_at` | `source.origin` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code sessions | `abstractnote import claude-sessions DIR` | human-typed prompt (the operator's words; the final assistant text of that turn is its outcome); one note per session summary (title, compaction and away summaries); one note per subagent run (its brief and its last report); one note per curated memory file | the record timestamp; a memory file: see [Dates](#dates) | `{session_id, uuid, prompt_id, cwd, git_branch, model, file, line, outcome, outcome_author}` |
| Agora hub | `abstractnote import agora DB` | recorded decision (`store decision:*`), claim and work entry, resolved or answered thread (root plus replies), operator message | `created_at` (a store entry without a message: its `updated_at`) | `{message_id, channel, seq, sender, reply_to, status, hash, retracted_at?}` |
| Markdown tree | `abstractnote import markdown DIR` | file (ADRs, backlog items, notes), with front-matter and headings kept | see [Dates](#dates) | `{repo, path, blob_sha, commit, added_as?, completed?}` |
| Files | `abstractnote import files PATH...` | file (documents, images, audio, video, logs) | the file's own metadata date (EXIF, XMP, PDF `CreationDate`, Office `core.xml` created), else the file date | `{path, sha256}` |

Every `source.origin` also carries `date_basis`: how `occurred_at` was found.

## Dates

| `date_basis` | Meaning | Approximate |
|---|---|---|
| `record` | the transcript record's own timestamp (prompts, summaries) | no |
| `first_record` / `last_record` | a subagent run's first record / a session title's last record | `last_record` yes |
| `message` | the agora message's `created_at` (threads, operator messages, store entries naming a message) | no |
| `store_updated` | an agora store entry that names no message: its `updated_at` | yes |
| `origin_session` | a memory file: the first record of its origin session (front matter `originSessionId`, looked up in the same project folder, then its sibling project folders) | yes (within that session) |
| `front_matter_modified` | a memory file whose origin session is not on disk: its front matter `modified` | yes (last edit) |
| `front_matter` | a Markdown front matter `date`, `created` or `created_at` | no |
| `created_line` | a Markdown `Created:` field line anywhere in the file (`- **Created:** 2026-09-12`) | no |
| `date_line` | a Markdown `Date:` field line in the first 40 lines (later ones date completion reports) | no |
| `git_added` | the commit that first added the file, following moves (`git log --follow --diff-filter=A`); also when that commit is earlier than the file's `Created:` line | yes |
| `bulk_commit` | the file was first added by a bulk import commit (10 or more files first added in the same second, `markdown.BULK_COMMIT_FILES`) and has no field line: the earlier of its modification time and that commit | yes |
| `exif` | a photo's EXIF `DateTimeOriginal` (else `DateTime`; Pillow, when installed) | no |
| `xmp` | an XMP creation date in an image or a PDF (`xmp:CreateDate`, `photoshop:DateCreated`, `exif:DateTimeOriginal`) | no |
| `pdf_created` | a PDF's Info `/CreationDate` | no |
| `office_created` | an Office Open XML document's `docProps/core.xml` `dcterms:created` (docx, xlsx, pptx) | no |
| `file_mtime` | the file's modification time | yes |

Files and captures share one detector, `abstractnote.ingest.dates.detect_file_date(path or bytes, mime)`: images
`exif` then `xmp`, PDFs `pdf_created` then `xmp`, Office documents `office_created`, then (for a path) `file_mtime`.
A capture that gives no `occurred_at` takes the first attachment's metadata date and records its basis. Two bases
are written after import (data-model.md "Time"): `content` when processing found the date the text states
itself on a note whose date was approximate (`note.redate`), and `user` when a person set the date; a live note's
basis is `client`, and an import from before date bases were recorded reads as `unrecorded` (approximate).

The order for a memory file is `origin_session`, `front_matter_modified`, `git_added`,
`file_mtime`; for a Markdown file `front_matter`, `created_line` (or `git_added` when the first commit is
earlier than that line), `date_line`, `git_added`, `file_mtime`. A commit that first added 10 or more files in
the same second is an import of an existing tree, not the files' creation: its files without a field line get
`bulk_commit` instead of `git_added`. An approximate date never makes anything old, quiet or stale in reflect
(cognition.md "note-reflect"). A field line is a labelled metadata line (an optional list marker and bold around
the label) whose value starts with an ISO date. A Markdown `Completed:` field line is kept as
written in `source.origin.completed` (`2026-09-27`), ready to be stated as a fact; `N/A` is not
kept. `added_as` is the path the file was first added under, when it has moved since.

## Memory folders

A Claude Code curated memory folder (`<project>/memory/*.md` of a `~/.claude/projects` folder: the project
folder holds session transcripts or sits in `~/.claude/projects`) belongs to the `claude-sessions` importer.
`abstractnote import markdown` on such a folder hands each file over (`claude_sessions.memory_draft`), so both
importers give the same importer and source key (`memory:<project>:<file>:<content hash>`) and the second
import of a file is a duplicate; `MEMORY.md`, the index, is never a note. Pairs written before that rule (a
`markdown` note and a `claude-sessions` memory note with the same file name and content hash) are archived
by `abstractnote dedupe-sources --notebook DIR [--dry-run] [--account NAME]`: the later received copy of
each pair, in ONE revision of `note.archive` ops naming the copy kept (`duplicate_of`); a waiting copy leaves
the queue. A second run finds nothing.

## Prompt notes

A prompt note is the operator's prompt, with `source.author` the operator. The assistant's final
text for that turn is `source.origin.outcome`, by `source.origin.outcome_author` (the model id).
It is also appended to the text after a separator that names the model (`---` then
`## Assistant answer (<model id>)`), so a search finds it without it being the operator's words.

## Agora selection

`--kinds decision,claim,work,thread,operator` picks what to write (default: all). Notes are cut
the same way whatever the selection (an operator reply inside an answered thread stays part of
that thread), so imports of separate kinds add up to one full import. `--include-channels a,b`
(also `--channels`) keeps only those channels; `--exclude-channels a,b` leaves those out.
Retracted messages are left out unless `--include-retracted` is given; a kept one carries
`retracted_at`. Left-out records are counted in `skipped` by reason (`kind_filtered_<kind>`,
`channel_filtered`, `channel_excluded`, `retracted`).

Rules shared by all importers:

- Skip machine noise: tool results, hook output, system reminders, presence and silence alerts,
  file-change notices. Keep what a person or an agent wrote on purpose.
- Keep whole texts. Large texts are sectioned at processing time, never truncated.
- Attach images by hash and type; do not inline bytes into notes.
- Mark the author: `source.author` is the account name, the agent seat, or the model name.
- Private content stays in the notebook; importers never post or copy anything outside it.
- Report counts (notes created, duplicates skipped, attachments stored, notes by kind, records
  skipped by reason), the time range covered, and the `date_basis` histogram with
  `approximate_dates` (how many dates are a session start, a last edit, a commit or a file date), in
  a dry run too, so a user sees how many dates are approximate before writing anything.

## Re-imports after the 2026-10-19 date and outcome fixes

Note ids derive from the source key, and none of the source keys changed: prompts
(`<session>:<uuid>`), memory files (`memory:<project>:<file>:<content hash>`), Markdown files
(`<repo>:<path>:<content hash>`) and agora entries keep their ids. A re-import into a notebook that
already holds them therefore reports duplicates and keeps the notes as they were (old dates, the
answer under `## Outcome` in the text, no `date_basis`); the corrected dates, outcome fields and
date bases reach a notebook only through a fresh import into a new notebook.

Every importer takes `--notebook DIR`, `--since`, `--until` and `--dry-run` (count only, write
nothing) and prints a counts report as JSON; the full flag list is in [api.md](api.md#cli). A
notebook pinned to an embedding server is opened with the same `--embed-base-url` and
`--embed-model` that `capture` and `process` take
([troubleshooting.md](troubleshooting.md#this-notebooks-vectors-were-made-with-the-embedding-model-)).

Processing an import runs through the same `note-process` flow as live notes. Expect roughly two
model calls per note; with a small local model this is a few seconds per note, so a corpus of a
few thousand notes takes hours. Run `abstractnote process --local` on the machine that holds the
model, or let the gateway's processor automation drain the queue over time.

---

## CONTRIBUTING.md

# Contributing to AbstractNote

Thank you for helping. This page covers the development setup, the tests, the generated flows and
the rules that keep the product consistent. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)
first; the HTTP, tool and CLI contracts are in [docs/api.md](docs/api.md), and the design
decisions in [docs/adr/](docs/adr/README.md).

## Development environment

Clone the framework packages next to this repository (the AbstractFramework `scripts/clone.sh`
does this) and install them editable into one virtual environment, so changes in a sibling
package are picked up without a release:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -e ../abstractsemantics -e ../abstractcore -e ../abstractruntime \
                      -e ../abstractmemory
.venv/bin/pip install -e ../abstractgateway      # for gateway work: 0.15.11 or later
.venv/bin/pip install -e ".[dev]"
```

Prefer the sibling checkouts over released packages, so a change in a sibling is tested before it
is released. The checkouts must meet the floors in `pyproject.toml` and the gateway's own: AbstractGateway
0.15.11 needs AbstractRuntime 0.10.6 or later, so an older `abstractruntime` checkout cannot host the
gateway tests; install the released `abstractruntime` instead until it moves.

## Tests

```sh
.venv/bin/pytest -q                                # the Python suite (scripted models, no weights)
.venv/bin/python -m abstractnote.flows.build --check
cd web && npm install && npm test && npm run build # web app: vitest, type check, build
cd watch/apple && scripts/build.sh                 # watch app: package tests, simulator build, screenshots
```

- Python tests use scripted models and the built-in hashing embedder; they never load a model.
  The gateway tests run when `abstractgateway` is installed and are skipped otherwise.
- A test that spawns processes must give them a scratch `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and `HF_HOME`.
- A scratch gateway for manual checks: `scripts/hermetic_gateway.sh start|status|stop` (ports
  18800-18899, scratch data directory, scripted model); see
  [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md#try-it-on-a-private-scratch-gateway).
- Every check you add must fail when the thing it checks is removed. Delete it once and watch the
  test go red.

## Flows

The flow JSON in `src/abstractnote/flows/json/` is generated. Edit the generator
(`src/abstractnote/flows/build.py`, `graph.py`), the prompts (`src/abstractnote/process/prompts/`)
or the schemas (`src/abstractnote/process/schemas.py`), then regenerate and commit the JSON:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m abstractnote.flows.build          # write
.venv/bin/python -m abstractnote.flows.build --check  # exit 1 when the JSON is stale
.venv/bin/abstractnote bundle --out dist/             # pack abstractnote@<version>.flow
```

Flows use catalog node types only. Every tool call is visible as its own nodes, and a tool's
failure ends the run with the tool's own sentence.

## Rules

- **No text heuristics for meaning.** Regular expressions or keyword lists never decide identity,
  intent or meaning. Deterministic code produces exact hashes and candidates; models decide
  ([ADR 0004](docs/adr/0004-models-decide-identity-no-text-heuristics.md)).
- **Tools stay bookkeeping.** Judgement lives in `llm_call` nodes with structured output; note
  tools hash, store, look up and apply ([ADR 0002](docs/adr/0002-flows-carry-cognition-tools-carry-bookkeeping.md)).
  Tools raise `ValueError` with one plain sentence on bad input and never log secrets.
- **Isolation.** Clients never send user, tenant or runtime identifiers; inside a gateway, tools
  never accept filesystem paths.
- **End-user copy.** In the web and watch apps: plain verbs; one-sentence errors; no system words
  such as ledger, run, gateway, workflow, record, and no ids; switches are labelled by the feature
  they control; actions sit at the bottom; nothing consequential happens without a tap. The web
  app's `test/copy.test.ts` checks the view strings.
- **Docs follow the code.** When you change behaviour, update the page that owns it (see
  [docs/README.md](docs/README.md)) and regenerate `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` in the same
  change. User-visible changes go in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

## Pull requests

Keep a pull request to one concern, include the tests that prove it, and say in the description
which documents changed. Report security issues privately as described in
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), not in a pull request or issue.

---

## SECURITY.md

# Security Policy

AbstractNote keeps personal notes, files and the knowledge drawn from them. Please report
vulnerabilities privately so they can be fixed before public disclosure.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Do **not** open a public issue for a security report. Use GitHub's private **Report a
vulnerability** form on the AbstractNote repository, or write to contact@abstractcore.ai.

Please include:

- a description of the issue and its impact;
- the affected component (core library, flows, gateway integration, web app, watch app, importers)
  and file paths if known;
- steps to reproduce or a minimal proof of concept;
- the version (`abstractnote status` shows it) and your environment;
- a suggested fix, if you have one.

We acknowledge reports as promptly as we can and agree a disclosure timeline with you.

## Supported versions

AbstractNote is alpha. Security fixes go to the `main` branch and the latest release on PyPI
and npm.

## Security model

These are the guarantees the design makes; a way around any of them is a vulnerability.

- **Per-user isolation.** Inside AbstractGateway every request is authenticated by the gateway
  and routed to the caller's own data plane; the notebook lives under that plane. Clients never
  send user, tenant or runtime identifiers, and an id from another notebook answers 404.
- **No filesystem paths inside the gateway.** The note tools read attachments only from files
  uploaded through the gateway (`{"$artifact": id}` from the host's artifact store). A path in a
  capture is refused. Headless use accepts paths only inside a folder the caller allows
  explicitly.
- **Auto-approved tools touch only your notebook.** The note tools are auto-approved because each
  one is bound to the caller's notebook and to nothing else.
- **Accounts.** Clients sign in with a `user` account token or an emailed one-time code; admin
  tokens are not meant for clients. The note tools never print or log secrets.
- **Importers read, never write, their sources.** The agora importer opens the hub database
  read-only; importers copy nothing outside the notebook.
- **Apple clients** keep the sign-in in one protected file in the app container (Data Protection,
  excluded from backup, deleted on sign-out), not in the OS keychain. This storage is proposed and
  awaits a ruling ([ADR 0006](docs/adr/0006-apple-client-credential-storage.md)).

## What you should protect

- The notebook is plain SQLite files and attachment blobs on disk, not encrypted by AbstractNote.
  Protect the gateway's data directory (or your `--notebook` directory) with the operating
  system's file permissions and disk encryption.
- Imports can bring private material (sessions, messages, documents) into a notebook. Import
  only what the notebook's owner may hold.

---

## CHANGELOG.md

# Changelog

All notable user-visible changes to AbstractNote are listed here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) and versions follow
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [Unreleased]

### Changed
- **What a thing is**: the description of a person, project or tool now says what it is (its kind,
  its role or purpose, and what it belongs to or works with), with the date of a fact that can
  change, instead of the latest thing that happened to it. It is rewritten only when a note changes
  what the thing is, and a note dated before what the notebook learned later describes the thing
  as it stood then.
- **Statements**: understanding a note now names how two things relate with a specific verb (runs
  on, depends on, fixed in, status, version) read from the first to the second, and keeps the same
  wording for the same kind of fact, so a new status or version replaces the old one.
- **Agents and their packages**: an agent that writes messages (such as a seat named `gateway`) is
  kept apart from the software it works on, even when both carry the same name.
- **One spelling per topic**: `abstractnote normalize-topics` joins only topics that differ by case,
  hyphens, underscores or spaces; a plural (`bug_fixes`) stays its own topic.
- **Nothing left out without a word** (ADR 0007): a description longer than 600 characters or a
  theme name longer than 4 words is kept whole with a warning instead of being cut or dropped;
  topics a note could not keep are named in what processing did to it; lists chosen under a bound
  (the graph, recall packets, search, stats, reflection candidates) say how much they left out, and
  a request for more than a read allows is answered and logged.

### Fixed
- **Consolidation no longer stops silently**: when the model gives an empty or partial answer, the
  consolidation asks once more, sets aside what is still unanswered for the next pass and goes on,
  instead of ending the summaries stage and calling the pass complete with hundreds of summaries
  still waiting. A pass that could not refresh everything is marked as having gaps, and the
  Processing page says so in one quiet line ("12 summaries could not be refreshed this time; they
  will be tried again next time.").

## [0.1.1] - 2026-10-19

Install with `pip install "abstractnote[gateway]"` (AbstractGateway 0.15.11 or later carries the
AbstractNote integration); the web app is `@abstractframework/note` on npm.

### Added
- **Watch**: a redesigned app on the wrist: one large field with a round mic and a Send capsule,
  the state line Sending → Received → Organizing → Organized with a haptic on Received, a result card
  with the kind, the title and tappable linked entities; Ask answers instantly by default (Quick) with
  Standard one tap away and sources as rows; Today shows what changed since you last looked, one cue
  at a time, the largest themes and open loops; entity and theme pages with "How it evolved".

- **Themes**: the notebook finds the groups of things your notes keep bringing together (a project
  and its people, a set of tools, a recurring subject) without a model, and the weekly reflection
  names each one in a few words with one sentence on what holds it together. A theme keeps its name
  while it changes little and is named again when it has changed a lot. `GET /note/communities`
  lists them, `POST /note/communities/recompute` finds them again on request, and every entity
  card says which theme it belongs to. Notes that mention many things count for less, so one long
  note rarely forms a theme by itself (a theme held together by that note's own statements still can).
- **Numbers**: `GET /note/stats` counts what the notebook has gathered: notes by kind and by where
  they came from, attachments, weekly activity over its whole span, people, projects and ideas,
  statements and how many were replaced, open and closed actions, insights, themes, processing, and
  the entities that have gone quiet.
- **Web app, Overview**: Explore opens on an Overview of the notebook: five figures (notes
  understood and waiting, people projects and ideas, beliefs and how many were replaced, open
  actions, themes), notes per week over the last 16 weeks with the busy weeks marked, entries by
  kind and the most noted ones, a card per theme that opens the picture with that theme alone, what
  has gone quiet, and processing in words.
- **Web app, picture**: nodes take their theme's colour, with a legend that shows one theme alone;
  hovering a node or a link fades the rest, and a card beside it (also on keyboard focus) gives its
  name, kind, one sentence, how many notes, first and latest, its theme and its three strongest
  links in words, drawn on top and never over the node or its neighbours. Link words appear when
  you zoom in.
- **Web app, how an entry evolved**: an entity's history opens with a line of what was said about
  it, week by week (month by month past half a year), with a marker and a date on each period where
  a belief was replaced.
- **Apple Watch app**: sign in on the watch with your user name or email, then a token or the
  8-digit code sent to you, on a screen that also sets the server; a server that cannot transcribe
  voice says so in one sentence and keeps the recording, so it can be sent as it is.

### Changed

- **Entities**: every entity has one canonical name, shown everywhere: lower case, with spaces and
  punctuation as one underscore (`Laurent-Philippe Albou` is `laurent_philippe_albou`), so `Memory`
  and `memory` are one entity, never two; the first way a note wrote it stays available as
  `display_name`. A new mention with a name the notebook already has is filed under that entity,
  whatever the model decided. An older notebook joins its same-name entities when it next processes a
  note, or on request with `abstractnote normalize` or `POST /note/entities/normalize` (`--dry-run`
  lists them first); each join can be undone. Different names for one thing (`Gateway` and
  `abstractgateway`) stay a matter for the model and your review.
- **Capture**: reading a notebook never changes it. Capture, quick filing, your own actions and
  archiving first finish any change a stopped process left half applied; `abstractnote recover`
  does it on request.
- **Understanding**: every model step has a fixed output budget and a known thinking setting
  (quick filing and naming themes without thinking); thinking for extraction and linking is chosen
  per run: on when a note is processed on its own, off by default for the background processing of
  a queue or an import (`thinking` on note-process and note-drain). Long
  notes are read in 6000-character sections; a section with text whose extraction finds nothing is
  read once more, and a second empty answer is marked on the note. The prompts start with the same
  instructions for every note, and the linking step sees a short list of candidates per name, so
  prompts are several times smaller and a note is understood faster. The prompts show an entity's
  kind after a dash (`memory — software`) and a name that still arrives with its kind in parentheses
  (`memory (software)`) is filed under the name alone; `abstractnote normalize` joins the entries an
  earlier version created that way into the entity they name.
- **Understanding**: a name becomes an entity only when it occurs in the note and is something you
  would look up again (ids, values, versions and generic words stay text); an existing entity is
  reused only for the very same thing (a part, version or feature of it is a new one); one to three
  topics per note; a statement the note replaces is closed rather than kept beside the new one;
  a missing entity summary is a warning, never a failed note.
- **Understanding**: contradiction candidates are only statements the linking marks as disputing
  each other, so several people or parts of one thing are no longer offered as contradictions.
- **Recall**: quick search keeps an entity or statement only when it matches the question well and a
  returned note carries it, groups hits under their notes with first and latest dates, and lists
  notes oldest first with `--order earliest` (`order=earliest` on `GET /note/search`).
- **Recall**: the standard answer reads a packet of bounded size (24,000 characters by default):
  the entities you asked about, the notes with excerpts around your question, and the history of
  their statements, instead of everything the graph reaches.
- **Recall**: open loops say how many days they have been open and are marked stale after 60 days
  (`GET /note/tasks`, `note_open_loops`).
- **Web app**: sign-in uses the framework's own dialog (gateway address, account, token, keep me
  signed in), remembers the last address and account, and the top-right corner has appearance,
  About, Settings and Connect/Disconnect. A gateway without AbstractNote shows one sentence,
  "AbstractNote is not installed on this gateway.", in every view.
- **Web app**: the Explore picture zooms (wheel, trackpad, pinch), pans, lets you drag a node while
  the layout settles around it, and fits to view on load or double-click; an empty notebook invites
  the first note or an import; organized notes lead with their title and linked entities.
- **Apple Watch app**: Settings show the server and account and sign out; tap to talk transcribes,
  or sends the recording as it is; errors are one specific sentence.
- **Importers**: a prompt note's author is the person who wrote the prompt, with the assistant's
  answer recorded as such; `import agora` selects by `--kinds`, `--include-channels` and
  `--exclude-channels` and can keep retracted entries with `--include-retracted`; every imported
  note records how its date was found, and import reports count the approximate dates.
- **Install**: the documentation describes the published packages; installing from source checkouts
  is the contributor path.

### Fixed

- **Processing after an upgrade**: the background processing and the weekly reflection kept the
  version of AbstractNote they were set up with, so after an upgrade notes stayed queued. Opening
  the web app now repairs them (or press Repair in Settings, Queue; `POST /note/processor/ensure`
  through the API), keeping your schedules and a paused state; `GET /note/status` and
  `GET /note/queue` say whether each one can run. The same repair applies when a new version adds or
  removes a tool the processing uses ("The tool list changed."), and the Apple Watch app runs it at
  launch and after each sign-in.
- **Themes after a library upgrade**: the themes depended on the installed `networkx` release, so an
  upgrade could rename or drop some of them. AbstractNote now accepts only the tested releases
  (`networkx>=3.2,<3.7`), records the release each computation used, and after a change keeps every
  name that still fits, hands the others to the theme they overlap most to be named again, and
  lists what it did in the recompute answer.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-19

The first version: the `abstractnote` package on PyPI and the `@abstractframework/note` web app on npm;
it needs AbstractMemory 0.3.1 and, for the gateway seam, AbstractGateway 0.15.11. The App Store
publication of the phone app is pending.

### Added

- **Notebook**: notes with history time, place and provenance; attachments stored once per
  content; idempotent capture (a retried send answers `duplicate`); notes that repeat or resemble
  earlier ones are linked to them as revisits.
- **Understanding**: quick filing (title, kind, topics, urgency, language), then extraction,
  candidate lookup and model-decided linking of entities, claims and tasks, applied as revisions
  to a note index and an AbstractMemory triple store. Facts are superseded, never overwritten;
  the graph and the beliefs at any past moment can be read back.
- **Queue**: priorities (urgent, high, normal, bulk), leases, retries after one and ten minutes,
  failed notes visible with their error and a retry action.
- **Flows**: `note-capture`, `note-process`, `note-drain`, `note-recall`, `note-mine` and
  `note-reflect` in the `abstractnote` bundle, editable in the Flow editor and runnable
  headlessly; `note-recall` also answers the `abstractcode.agent.v1` chat contract.
- **Recall**: quick (full-text plus vector, no model), standard (graph expansion and one cited
  synthesis), deep (a stored dossier); since-you-last-looked changes, cue cards, entity cards as
  of a moment, then-versus-now, relation timelines, evidence chains, day and timeline views.
- **Reflection**: open loops, contradictions, resurfacing and anniversaries turned into insights
  on a schedule; the first one runs a full interval after the notebook is set up (opening an
  empty notebook never starts a model), or at once with "Reflect now".
- **User actions**: close a task, retract a claim, undo a merge, acknowledge an insight, archive
  a note; each one is a revision with the account as its source. A claim you retract was never
  true; "since you last looked" lists it as withdrawn, in plain words.
- **Gateway integration** (with the AbstractGateway integration): per-user note tools,
  auto-approved; the note read API under `/api/gateway/note`; the processor and reflect
  automations through `POST /note/processor/ensure`; the Note app in the gateway's app catalog.
- **Web app** `@abstractframework/note`: Capture, Remember and Explore, with a Settings panel.
- **Apple Watch app**: Note, Ask, Today and Settings; watch-only, watchOS 26 or later.
- **Command line** `abstractnote`: capture, search, entity, day, status, changes, rebuild,
  process, bundle and import, on a notebook directory.
- **Importers**: Claude Code sessions, an agora hub database (read-only), Markdown trees and
  files, with original dates, provenance and `--dry-run` counts.

### Requirements

- AbstractMemory 0.3.1 or later; AbstractGateway 0.15.11 or later for the gateway path.

---
